The comparison of the means of the different treatments and the statistical significance of the effects of the main factors and their second and third order interactions, respectively, were carried out by carrying out a multifactorial variance analysis of the IM with the statistical program (software) Minitab 14. Results and discussion The concentrations for each metal, as well as the total concentrations for each sampling point are presented in Table 1. Analyzed, concentrations for each metal are related to each other as follows: PB> CR, CD> HG. The sampling of the month of May (rainy season) presented the total higher heavy metal concentrations, with concentrations that fluctuate between 237.2 and 173.5 µg/l. As for the sampling point, it was found that the largest total concentration of the metals analyzed was on the Juanchito bridge (237.2 µg/l), the El Hormiguero bridge (205.05 µG/L), and the South Collector Channel (181.41 µg/L). The results of the mutagenicity tests are presented in Table 2. The mutagenicity tests generated positive immers only in the month of May with the ta98 strain in the absence of the treatment of metabolic activation at the points: El Hormiguero bridge, mouth of the South Collector Channel and mouth of the Cali River, with IM of 3.6, 2.9 and 2.7 respectively. On the other hand, the IMs obtained in the presence of the metabolic activation system threw values ​​that range between 1.6 and 1.8 for all points. As for the ta100 strain, a higher, not positive response was observed, with the metabolic activation treatment. In the months of August and September, IMS were not obtained. By August, the ta98 and TA100 strains presented a similar behavior against the metabolic activation treatment. The IM proved to be significantly lower in the absence of mixture S9. In September, IM for both strains and levels of metabolic activation treatment were similar, varying between 1.2 and 1.6. The statistical analysis indicates that there is a significant interaction on the IM (P-value <0.05), for the factors of sampling and strain of S. Typhimurium, being the sampling time (temporary component) the factor that most contributes to the explanation of the total variability of the IM. On the contrary, the sampling point factors (spatial component) and metabolic activation treatment did not generate significant differences between the means of their treatments. Regarding the interactions between main factors, there are second order units, statistically significant, between the effects of the sampling month, sampling month-metabolic treatment and metabolic strain-treatment, as well as in the interaction of the third order month of sampling-cepa-metabolic treatment, not being so for the rest of the interactions studied. According to the multiple comparison procedure of the lowest significant differences of Fischer (LSD) carried out to determine if the means per time of sampling were significantly different, it was found that the months of August and September (dry season) behaved as two homogeneous groups, since their means did not present statistically significant differences. Figure 2 clearly shows the differences between May (rainy season), and August and September (dry season) with respect to the average IM. It is evident that in the month of May 2013 (rainy season) the highest total heavy metal concentrations (Table 1) were presented, coinciding with the highest IMS registered in this study (Table 2). A possible explanation why the month of May obtained the highest total metal concentrations, could be found in the river flow at the time of sampling, since in the rainy season of 2013, the water level of the river reached values ​​above the historical averages of the time, generating an alteration in the chemical exchange between the sediment and the water column, and an increase in the increase in the concentration of suspended solids suspended runoff.                     Although the 90 of heavy metals in aquatic systems is associated with suspended matters and sediments, chemical exchange between unaltered sediment and water column is little and slow; A disturbance or modification of the sediment can increase the exchange between them, accelerating the exchange of the contaminants between the sediment and the water column (16). On the contrary, in August and September 2013 (dry season), a decrease in the levels for the entire basin was reported and the values ​​remained in the range of historical media for that time of the year.      With respect to the total concentration of metals at each point and their behavior throughout the three mThese sampling, it was found that the mouth of the South Collecting Canal proved to be the most homogeneous sampling point, presenting total concentrations between 118 and 181 µg/l. The above makes sense taking into account that the channel has historically been exposed to the continuous discharges of wastewater from the drainage-south system of the city of Cali and receives leachates from the old Navarro garbage deposit site. The ta98 and TA100 strains exhibited a significant effect as a main factor, in the interaction with the sampling months, as seen in Figure 3. Both responded similarly to the extracts of the months of September and August (dry season), whose total concentrations of heavy metal are considered intermediate and low, respectively (see Table 2).           As the total value of the concentration of heavy metals increased, according to the sampling month, the average IM for each strain increased its magnitude, being greater for the ta98 strain. On the other hand, in the face of the highest concentrations in the month of May, the ta100 strain declines, indicating a greater sensitivity to concentrations greater than 120 µg/l, coinciding with what was previously reported (17), where it is stated that the genetic background of the ta100 strain seems to be more sensitive to the mortal effects of the chemicals than that of the ta98 strain. The second significant interaction was among the factors of sampling and treatment of metabolic activation. As seen in Figure 4, treatments with and without mix S9 behave in the same way in the months of May and September (high and intermediate concentrations respectively) observing a superior IM without S9, in both cases. In August (low concentrations) treatment without S9 exhibits an average IM much lower than that obtained in the presence of enzymatic activator. This result could be due to the highest total average concentration for HG in the month of August, (11.92 µg/l) compared to May (7.87 µg/l) and September (5.29 µg/l). HG is heavy metal with the most powerful toxicity and has been found to have a minimal inhibitory concentration of 0.01 mm in Escherichia coli (18). In August, the total average concentration for HG was 0.012 mm, triggering a possible toxic effect on most sampling points. In the absence of the enzymatic activator, the HG ions present in the extract have a greater bioavailability during the development of the test and therefore greater toxicity. On the contrary, the toxic effect was attenuated by the presence of the S9 mixture, since the metalloproteins present in the homogenized liver have the ability to join cadmium, copper, mercury and zinc ions (7). The union of heavy metals to these proteins decreases the union of metals to DNA residues. The above explains the low average index values ​​in the presence of Mix S9 compared to those observed in its absence, especially for the month of May.           The last second order significant interaction of the factors Straight and treatment of metabolic activation is presented in Figure 5; Ta98 and TA100 strains respond in a completely different way to treatments with and without mixture S9. The average IM of the ta98 strain increases in the absence of enzymatic activator and slightly decays in its presence. On the contrary, the average IM of the ta100 strain increases in the presence of the S9 mixture and decreases in its absence. As already mentioned, the TA100 strain is more sensitive to toxicity due to the presence of heavy metals in the extracts, increasing the average values ​​as it is in the presence of the S9 mixture. This is because by reducing the bioavailability of metal ions, its synergistic toxic effect is decreased, allowing greater survival of the bacterial population and therefore, a greater capacity for responseto. For the ta98 strain, which has turned out to be more resistant, the S9 enzymatic activator remains bioavailability and allows bacteria to have a lower interaction with metal ions, a situation that does not happen in the absence of S9. Finally, and according to the analysis of the effect of the third order interaction between the month of sampling-cepa-metabolic activation treatment, the largest average IM of 2.5, belongs to the effect resulting from the interaction between the high total concentrations of the month of May (rainy season) and the ta98 strain without metabolic activation, significantly differentiating from the rest of the treatments. This indicates that the high concentration of total heavy metals triggered reading change mutations, mainly in the absence of a metabolic activation system, a situation that agrees with most surface water studies around the world, in which there is a predominance of mutagens of reading change (detected by the TA98), instead of mutagen of replacement of base pairs (detected by the TA100) (9) (9) (9). In general, the factor that contributes the most to the explanation of the total variability of the IM is the month of sampling, followed by the interaction between the sampling month and the strain of S. Typhimurium. With respect to sampling sites, it was found that in general the points have a mild to moderate mutagenic activity, as previously established (6). When analyzing the recommended limit values ​​and established by the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) for heavy metals in surface waters, it is possible to conclude that the high total concentration of heavy metals, in the month of May it could trigger a significant mutagenic activity, since the average total concentrations for each metal exceed the allowed values ​​(4).           Conclusions The work done allows us to conclude that the space-time variation of the mutagenic effect of heavy metals present in the waters of the Cauca River during 2013, expressed through the IM, receives a significant contribution of the sampling time, the temporal component, and not of the different sampling points, the spatial component. This indicates that the variation of environmental conditions when passing the rainy season to the dry season would be influencing not only the dynamics and behavior of heavy metal concentrations in the Cauca River, but also the probability of significant mutagenic effects on biological communities and surrounding populations. Chronic contamination by heavy metals such as the one that has historically experienced the Cauca River, ends up producing notable alterations in the composition and structure of organisms that live in river courses. It should be remembered that sometimes changes in concentrations of the order of micrograms per liter to produce appreciable effects on the structure and functioning of biological communities. title: ¿Qué hay tras hallazgos de esqueletos de caballos en el ...
snippet: 29/07/2024 — ¿Qué hay tras hallazgos de esqueletos de caballos en el río Cauca en Cali? ... La Personería de Santiago de Cali solicitó una intervención ...
trans_snippet: 07/29/2024 - What is after findings of horse skeletons in the Cauca River in Cali? ... the Personería de Santiago de Cali requested an intervention ...
text: La Personería de Santiago de Cali solicitó una intervención por parte de las autoridades tras descubrir sitios presuntamente utilizados para el sacrificio de caballos en la ribera del río Cauca. Este hallazgo se realizó durante un operativo de control, vigilancia y verificación en conjunto con las personerías de Yumbo y Palmira. En el marco de la inspección, se encontraron restos de caballos en dos ubicaciones situadas en el margen izquierdo del río, abarcando las comunas 6 y 7 de Cali. Gerardo Mendoza Castrillón, personero de Cali, enfatizó la importancia de que las autoridades competentes lleven a cabo una inspección detallada en los sitios descubiertos. “Es importante que las autoridades realicen una inspección a estos lugares para verificar este hecho a fin de encontrar los autores que hay detrás del repudiable acto que compromete la vida y la integridad física de los animales”, declaró Mendoza Castrillón. Según el personero, el sacrificio de caballos en estas condiciones no solo es inaceptable, sino que también plantea serios riesgos para la salud pública. Otros problemas ambientales El operativo también puso de manifiesto otros problemas ambientales significativos en la ribera del río Cauca. Durante la inspección, se observaron acumulaciones de escombros y descargas de aguas residuales industriales. Estas descargas afectaron las condiciones físico-químicas del agua del río, resultando en un oscurecimiento del cauce y la presencia de espuma en la cercanía de la estación de bombeo Paso del Comercio. Estos problemas podrían estar asociados con la posible presencia de coliformes en el agua, lo que intensifica la preocupación por la calidad del recurso hídrico. Los mataderos clandestinos, que operan sin las debidas regulaciones sanitarias, sacrifican caballos viejos y deteriorados. Este tipo de actividad no solo plantea un riesgo para la salud de los consumidores, sino que también contribuye a la proliferación de carne en condiciones insalubres. La falta de control en estos mataderos puede llevar a la comercialización de productos cárnicos que no cumplen con los estándares de seguridad alimentaria, afectando potencialmente a la población. Las autoridades de Cali, junto con sus homólogos de Yumbo y Palmira, fueron llamadas a tomar medidas inmediatas para abordar tanto el problema de los mataderos clandestinos como la contaminación ambiental detectada. La intervención rápida y efectiva es crucial para mitigar los daños a la salud pública y al medio ambiente.   Comments
text_en: The Personería de Santiago de Cali requested an intervention by the authorities after discovering sites allegedly used for the sacrifice of horses on the riverbank of the Cauca River. This finding was carried out during a control, surveillance and verification operation in conjunction with the Yumbo and Palmira personnel. Within the framework of the inspection, horse remains were found in two locations located on the left margin of the river, covering the communes 6 and 7 of Cali. Gerardo Mendoza Castrillón, Personero of Cali, emphasized the importance of competent authorities carrying out a detailed inspection in the discovered sites. "It is important that the authorities carry out an inspection of these places to verify this fact in order to find the authors behind the repudiable act that compromises the life and physical integrity of the animals," said Mendoza Castrillón. According to the Personero, the sacrifice of horses in these conditions is not only unacceptable, but also raises serious risks to public health. Other environmental problems The operation also showed other significant environmental problems on the riverbank of the Cauca River. During the inspection, accumulations of debris and discharges of industrial wastewater were observed. These discharges affected the physical-chemical conditions of the river water, resulting in a darkening channel and the presence of foam in the vicinity of the Paso del Comercio pumping station. These problems could be associated with the possible presence of coliforms in the water, which intensifies concern for the quality of water resource. Clandestine slaughterhouses, who operate without proper health regulations, sacrifice old and deteriorated horses. This type of activity not only raises a risk to the health of consumers, but also contributes to the proliferation of meat in unhealthy conditions. The lack of control in these slaughterhouses can lead to the commercialization of meat products that do not meet food safety standards, potentially affecting the population. The authorities of Cali, together with their counterparts from Yumbo and Palmira, were called to take immediate measures to address both the problem of clandestine slaughterhouses and the environmental pollution detected. The rapid and effective intervention is crucial to mitigate damage to public health and the environment.   Comments

text: Trong thời kỳ mùa khô chỉ có 2 trạm trên thượng nguồn (M7 và M8) vẫn có giá trị tổng Coliform nằm trong giới hạn cho phép của cột A. Tuy nhiên, tất cả các trạm khác còn lại đều có giá trị tổng Coliform đo được vượt tiêu chuẩn cột A (M1 và M2) và cột B (7,5x103 ≤ B ≤ 10x103 MPN/100ml). Giá trị tổng Coliform tại các trạm M3, M4, M5 và M6 đều vượt tiêu chuẩn cho phép của cột B, do vậy nguồn nước của các khu vực này bị ô nhiễm vi sinh khá nặng với các nguồn chủ yếu là chất thải sinh hoạt từ các khu dân cư tập trung, chất thải trong nông nghiệp và một số nhà máy ven sông thải trực tiếp vào nguồn nước. Nhận xét chung về hiện trạng chất lượng nước sông Cái Nha Trang: Qua kết quả khảo sát và phân tích cho thấy rằng nguồn nước của sông Cái Nha Trang hiện nay đã có nhiều biểu hiện bị ô nhiễm cục bộ từng khu vực và vào từng thời điểm trong năm. -  Vào thời kỳ mùa lũ (từ tháng 9 ÷ 11) thì toàn bộ nguồn nước trong sông đều bị đục và hàm lượng cặn tăng cao ảnh hưởng tới chất lượng nước cấp sinh hoạt và nuôi thủy sản; -  Vào giai đoạn mùa kiệt chỉ có một số đoạn sông bị ô nhiễm do chịu tác động của chất thải, nước thải từ các nguồn thải sinh hoạt, canh tác nông nghiệp, chất thải từ các nhà máy thải trực tiếp xuống sông gây ô nhiễm, đó là tại các vị trí lấy mẫu M2, M3, M4, M5; -  Ô nhiễm do hàm lượng FeTS cao trong nước chỉ xảy ra đối với doạn sông có các trạm đo: M2, M3 và M4. Đây là các điểm đo nằm ở phía hạ du chịu tác động của các nguồn thải các khu dân cư cũng như chất thải từ canh tác nông nghiệp trong vùng thải ra. Tuy nhiên, mức độ ô nhiễm không quá cao mà chỉ nằm trong giới hạn cột B (1,0 ≤ B ≤ 2,0 mg/l) theo quy chuẩn QCVN 08: 2008/BTNMT. Các nhánh sông từ giao điểm M4 trở về thượng nguồn là chưa bị ảnh hưởng do ô nhiễm FeTS trong nguồn nước; -  Ô nhiễm do vi sinh được thể hiện rõ tại các vị trí lấy mẫu M3, M4, M5 và M6 và đặc biệt cao tại vị trí M6 với giá trị đo được vượt cao gấp gần 6 lần so với tiêu chuẩn cho phép của cột B theo quy chuẩn QCVN 08: 2008/BTNMT sẽ ảnh hưởng rất nghiêm trọng tới việc sử dụng cấp nước cho sinh hoạt của người dân cũng như cho nuôi thủy sản. Những khu vực ô nhiễm vi sinh đều tập trung tại những vùng có dân cư tập trung đông, những vùng có kinh tế phát triển kinh tế cao của tỉnh Khánh Hòa. Do vậy, trong những năm tới cần phải có chế độ kiểm tra, giám sát tốt hơn cho những vị trí này và mở rộng thêm các điểm giám sát để xác định rõ nguyên nhân gây ô nhiễm nhằm đề xuất các giải pháp phù hợp giảm thiểu ô nhiễm vi sinh cho những khu vực bị ô nhiễm cao. 3. Đề xuất giải pháp bảo vệ nguồn nước sông Cái Nha Trang Từ các kết quả khảo sát, phân tích đánh giá nhóm tác giả đã đề xuất một số giải pháp giảm thiểu những tác động tới ô nhiễm nguồn nước sông Cái Nha Trang như sau: - Cần nạo vét, khơi thông dòng chảy đối với một số nhánh sông thuộc khu vực nội ô như nhánh sông Kim Bòng, hạn chế tình trạng ứ đọng rác thải, nước thải trong một thời gian dài;  - Các đập dâng mới xây dựng trên sông cần có thiết kế phù hợp, có hạng mục công trình xả đáy và vận hành thường xuyên nhằm giảm lượng trầm tích bùn đáy ô nhiễm tích tụ trong thời gian dài gây ô nhiễm nguồn nước, đồng thời gây thiếu hụt lượng cát cho vùng cửa sông và khu vực bãi tắm của vịnh Nha Trang; - Giải quyết dứt điểm các khu vực gây ô nhiễm môi trường nghiêm trọng trong khu dân cư, khu vực cửa sông Cái, đẩy nhanh việc thực hiện dự án đường và bờ kè sông Cái Nha Trang; - Cần quản lý tình trạng khai thác khoáng sản trái phép còn xảy ra ở nhiều địa phương nhất là khai thác cát trên các sông, khai thác đất san lấp, khai thác nước ngầm, đặc biệt gần đây xảy ra các vụ khai thác khoáng sản trên địa bàn huyện Khánh Vĩnh với mức hủy hoại và gây ô nhiễm môi trường một cách nghiêm trọng; - Giải quyết các khu vực gây ô nhiễm môi trường nghiêm trọng trong khu dân cư, khu vực cửa sông Cái, đẩy nhanh việc thực hiện dự án đường và bờ kè sông Cái Nha Trang; - Quy hoạch các khu giết mổ gia súc, gia cầm - Kiểm tra việc chấp hành pháp luật về bảo vệ môi trường đối với các dự án sau khi được phê duyệt báo cáo đánh giá tác động môi trường. Bản cam kết bảo vệ môi trường cần phải được thường xuyên giám sát thực hiện. - Giáo dục nhằm tăng cường ý thức chấp hành pháp luật về bảo vệ môi trường của một số doanh nghiệp, cơ sở sản xuất, kinh doanh - Bổ sung chế tài và lực lượng để xử phạt đối với các hành vi vi phạm pháp luật về bảo vệ môi trường ở mức độ nhỏ lẻ; - Tăng cường quan trắc, dự báo diễn biến chất lượng môi trường, xác định kịp thời các vấn đề môi trường cấp bách của tỉnh. Phân loại các cơ sở gây ô nhiễm môi trường nghiêm trọng, xử lý nghiêm các cơ sở vi phạm tiêu chuẩn môi trường; - Tăng cường đào tạo, tập huấn nâng cao trình độ chuyên môn, nghiệp vụ, quản lý về môi trường cho cán bộ công chức làm công tác bảo vệ môi trường. - Sớm xây dựng khung chương trình hành động đối với công tác bảo vệ môi trường cho từng giai đoạn phát triển, trong đó có sự lồng ghép các chương trình hành động quốc gia, phải phù hợp với định hướng quy hoạch, phát triển chung tỉnh. Bên cạnh đó thì các định hướng, quy hoạch về mặt môi trường sẽ làm cơ sở cho các định hướng pháp triển kinh tế, xã hội của tỉnh. 3. KẾT LUẬN VÀ KIẾN NGHỊ Từ kết quả phân tích đánh giá cho thấy: hiện nay nguồn nước sông Cái Nha Trang bắt đầu bị ô nhiễm cục bộ trên những vùng chịu nhiều tác động của các nguồn thải ảnh hưởng tới phát triển kinh tế - xã hội cho các địa phương trong vùng. Các tác giả đã phân tích, đánh giá nguyên nhân gây ô nhiễm từ đó đề xuất các giải pháp công trình và phi công trình khả thi nhằm giảm thiểu các tác nhân gây ô nhiễm để từng bước cải tạo chất lượng nước và bảo vệ môi trường. Để đảm bảo được yêu cầu cải thiện được chất lượng nước sông Cái và bảo vệ môi trường, chúng tôi kiến nghị cần thực hiện những nhiệm vụ sau trong những năm gần đây:  -  Rà soát, đánh giá rủi ro môi trường của việc phát triển công nghiệp trên toàn tỉnh Khánh Hòa; -  Đánh giá hiện trạng môi trường và tính toán khả năng chịu tải của các sông, suối chính trên toàn tỉnh Khánh Hòa; -  Xây dựng hệ thống quan trắc môi trường tự động tại các khu vực xung yếu của tỉnh Khánh Hòa;  [1]. Đài khí tượng thủy văn khu vực Nam Trung bộ, 2011. Báo cáo lập bản đồ ngập lụt khu vực sông Dinh Ninh hòa và sông Cái Nha Trang. [2]. Lương Văn Thanh và cs, 2012. Đánh giá hiện trạng môi trường lưu vực sông Cái (Nha Trang) và sông Dinh (Ninh Hòa), phân tích nguyên nhân và đề xuất các giải pháp bảo vệ và cải thiện môi trường. text_en: During the dry season, only 2 stations on the upstream (M7 and M8) still have a total coliform value within the permissible limits of column A. However, all other stations have the total value of coliform measured beyond column standard A (M1 and M2) and column B (7.5x103 ≤ B ≤ 10x103 MPN/100ml). The total value of coliform at M3, M4, M5 and M6 stations exceed the permitted standard of column B, so the water source of these areas is quite seriously polluted with microorganisms with main sources of domestic waste from centralized residential areas, agricultural waste and some riverside factories directly exhausted into the water source. General comments on the current status of the quality of Cai Nha Trang river water: Through the survey results and analysis shows that the water source of Cai Nha Trang River has now many signs of local pollution in each region and from time to time of the year. -During the flood season (from September ÷ 11), all water in the river were cloudy and the high level of sediment affected the quality of water supply and aquaculture; -In the period of exhausted season, there are only a few sections of polluted rivers due to the impact of waste and waste water from domestic waste sources, agricultural and waste farming from factories directly into the river, causing pollution, which is at the location of sampling M2, M3, M4, M5; -Pollution due to high fets in the water only occurs for rivers with measuring stations: M2, M3 and M4. These are the measurement points located on the downstream side affected by the sources of residential areas as well as waste from agricultural farming in the emissions. However, the level of pollution is not too high but only within the column limit B (1.0 ≤ B ≤ 2.0 mg/l) in accordance with QCVN 08: 2008/BTNMT. River branches from M4 intersection to upstream are not yet affected by FETS pollution in water sources; -Microbiological pollution is clearly shown at the sampling locations of M3, M4, M5 and M6 and especially high at the M6 ​​position with the measured value that is nearly 6 times higher than the permitted standard of column B in accordance with QCVN 08: 2008/BTNMT standards will seriously affect the use of water supply for the daily life of the people as well as for aquaculture. Microbiological pollution areas are concentrated in areas with concentrated population, areas with high economic development economy of Khanh Hoa province. Therefore, in the coming years, it is necessary to have a better inspection and supervision regime for these positions and expand the surveillance points to clearly identify the cause of pollution to propose appropriate solutions to minimize microbiological pollution for high polluted areas. 3. Proposing solutions to protect the water source of Cai Nha Trang river from survey results, analysis and evaluation of the author has proposed a number of solutions to minimize the impact on the pollution of Cai Nha Trang River water sources as follows: - It is necessary to dredge and clear the flow for some of the inner river branches such as the Kim Bong branch, limiting the stagnation of waste and waste water for a long time;  - Newly built rivers on the river need to have the appropriate design, have a site of bottom discharge and operate regularly to reduce the amount of polluted mud sediments accumulated for a long time causing water pollution, and cause a shortage of sand for the estuaries and beach areas of Nha Trang Bay; - Definitely solve areas causing serious environmental pollution in residential areas, Cai river estuary area, accelerate the implementation of the Cai Trang River Road and embankment project; - It is necessary to manage the status of illegal mineral exploitation that occurs in many localities, especially sand mining on rivers, exploit land leveling and exploiting underground water, especially recently occurred cases of mineral exploitation in Khanh Vinh district with serious destruction and pollution of environmental pollution; - Solving serious environmental pollution areas in residential areas, Cai river estuary area, accelerating the implementation of the Cai Nha Trang River Road and embankment project; - Planning of cattle and poultry slaughter areasU when approved for environmental impact assessment reports. The commitment of environmental protection needs to be regularly supervised. - Education to strengthen the awareness of law observance on environmental protection of a number of businesses, production and business establishments - Supplement sanctions and forces to sanction violations of law on environmental protection at a small level; - Enhancing monitoring and forecasting environmental quality changes, timely determining urgent environmental issues of the province. Classification of serious environmental pollution facilities, strictly handle establishments that violate environmental standards; - Strengthen training and training to improve professional qualifications and environmental management for civil servants in charge of environmental protection. - Early build an action program framework for environmental protection for each stage of development, including the integration of national action programs, must be consistent with the provincial planning and development orientation. In addition, environmental orientations and planning will be the basis for the provincial economic and social development orientations. 3. Conclusion and recommendations from the evaluation analysis results show that: At present, the water source of Cai Nha Trang river starts to be local pollution in areas affected by waste sources affecting socio -economic development for localities in the region. The authors have analyzed and assessed the causes of pollution from which to propose feasible works and pilots to minimize pollutants to gradually improve water quality and protect the environment. Utilização de indicadores biológicos na avaliação da qualidade da água da Baía do Guajará e do Rio Guamá (Belém-Pará). 2006. 72 f. Dissertação (Mestrado) - Universidade Federal do Pará, Núcleo de Ciências Agrárias e Desenvolvimento Rural, Empresa Brasileira de Pesquisa Agropecuária, Universidade Federal Rural da Amazônia, Belém, 2006. Programa de Pós-Graduação em Ciência Animal. Resumo:  Belém, a capital do estado do Pará, possui uma posição geográfica privilegiada devido a uma  vasta rede hidrográfica que permite a entrada de marés vinda da baía do Guajará e do rio  Guamá. Estes são importantes ecossistemas aquáticos para a região. O presente trabalho tem  como objetivo avaliar a qualidade da água da baía do Guajará e do rio Guamá através de  análises microbiológicas e da utilização de peixes como biomarcadores. Durante o estudo  foram feitas quatro coletas durante quatro períodos: intermediário chuvoso (dezembro/04),  chuvoso (março/05), intermediário seco (junho/05) e seco (setembro/05). Foram coletadas  100ml de água superficial em quatro pontos localizados na baía do Guajará (porto do Arapari,  Ver -o – Peso, igarapé do Una e ilha da Barra) e três pontos no rio Guamá (Linhão, igarapé do  Tucunduba e porto da Palha). A análise microbiológica foi feita de acordo com a descrição da  20ª edição do Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wasterwater (APHA,  1998). Para a analise de biomarcadores foram feitas pescarias experimentais e capturados um  total de 36 peixes da espécie Brachyplatystoma rousseauxii. Após a coleta foi feita análise  histológica do fígado. Os resultados das análises microbiológicas demonstraram que em seis  pontos de coleta as concentrações de coliformes totais e termotolerantes foram maiores  durante os períodos intermediário chuvoso e chuvoso, sendo que o ponto localizado na ilha da  Barra apresentou baixa concentração desses indicadores sanitários durante os quatro períodos  de coleta. A água da baía do Guajará e do rio Guamá de acordo com a portaria do CONAMA  Nº 357/ 2005 são águas pertencentes a classe três, no entanto elas apresentaram níveis de  coliformes totais e termotolerantes acima do limite estabelecido para esta classe de água, com  exceção do ponto localizado na ilha da Barra. A análise microbiológica sugere que a água da  baía do Guajará e do rio Guamá apresenta altos índices de contaminação fecal. Em relação a  análise dos fígados da espécie Brachyplatystoma rousseauxii os resultados demonstram que  nos locais de lançamentos de efluentes houve uma variação no número de indivíduos com  alterações do tecido hepático, sendo encontrados 24 peixes com alterações. O igarapé do Una  foi o local com maior número de peixes com fígados alterados. Os resultados encontrados  neste trabalho sugerem que o ambiente da baía do Guajará e do rio Guamá encontram-se em  início de degradação devido ao excesso de despejo de efluente doméstico e industrial que  representam um risco para o equilíbrio das comunidades aquáticas. Abstract:  Belém, of Pará has a hight hydrographic system, in this way is possible the entrance of tides  come from Guajará’s bay and of Guamá river. These are important aquatics ecosystems to the  region. The purpose of these research is to evaluate the quality of water from Guajará’s bay  and Guamá river, through of mycrobiologics and biomarkers analysis. During the research  were made four collects in four period: intermediate rainy( December/ 04), rainy( March/05),  intermediate dry (June/ 05) and dry (September/ 05). Sample 100 ml of surface-water were  collected in four places in Guajará’s bay ( Arapari’s harbor, Ver-O-Peso, Una´s River and  Barra’s Island) and three places in Guamá’s river ( Linhão, Tucunduba river, and Palha’s  harbor). The mycrobiologic analysis was done accordance with the description of 20th edition  of standard methods for the examination of water and wastewater (APHA, 1998). To the  analysis of biomarkers was captured Brachyplatystoma rousseauxii specie. After of collect we  did analysis histological analysis of livers. The result of the microbiological analysis showed  that in six places of the collect the concentration of total coliforms and termotolerants were  higher during the intermediate rainy period. During the four period of collect, Barra’s island  showed a less concentration of these domestic polution. In accordance with law CONAMA  357/2005, the water of Guajará’s bay and Guamá river belong to class three, but they have  more total colifoms and termotolerants than is determinate to this water´s class, however the  in Barra’s island was the exception. The microbiological analysis showed a high fecal  contamination in the Guajará’s bay and Guamá river. The result of analysis in the livers of  Brachyplatystoma rousseauxii specie showed variations in hepatic tissue of some this fishes  collected in places where the effluents are threw, we met 24 fishes with alteration. The Una’s  river had more fishes with alteration than others. The result of this studies showed that the  environment of Guajará’s bay and the Guamá river are in a initial degradation, because a lot  of domestics and industrial effluents are throw in this waters. It affects the balance of aquatics  community. These are important aquatic ecosystems forfor the region. The present study aims to evaluate the water quality of the Guajará Bay and the Guamá River through microbiological analyses and the use of fish as biomarkers. During the study, four collections were made during four periods: intermediate rainy (December/04), rainy (March/05), intermediate dry (June/05) and dry (September/05). 100 ml of surface water were collected at four points located in the Guajará Bay (Arapari port, Ver-o-Peso, Una stream and Barra island) and three points in the Guamá River (Linhão, Tucunduba stream and Palha port). After collection, histological analysis of the liver was performed. The results of the analyses wereMicrobiological analyses demonstrated that at six collection points the concentrations of total and thermotolerant coliforms were higher during the intermediate rainy and rainy periods, and the point located on Barra Island presented low concentrations of these health indicators during the four collection periods. Regarding the analysis of the livers of the species Brachyplatystoma rousseauxii, the results demonstrate that at the effluent discharge sites there was a variation in the number of individuals with alterations in the liver tissue, withthe 24 fish with alterations. The Una stream was the location with the largest number of fish with altered livers. The results found in this work suggest that the environment of the Guajará Bay and the Guamá River are in the beginning of degradation due to the excessive dumping of domestic and industrial effluents that represent a risk to the balance of aquatic communities. text: As águas superficiais do Rio Guamá, que serve para diversos usos, possuem valores elevados de coliformes termotolerantes, que são bactérias indicativas de contato da água com material de origem fecal. Ao que tudo indica os danos à qualidade da água estão sendo provocados devido à alta carga de poluição que chega ao rio. Dados da pesquisa mostram que a quantidade de coliformes termotolerantes ultrapassa o indicado pelas resolução do Conama, que seria até 1.000 nmp/100ml; pontos do Rio Guamá apresentaram valores acima do limite legal permitido como 12.098 nmp/100ml. Esses dados foram levantados pela Carla Renata Carneiro, advogada e licenciada em Biologia, mestra e doutoranda pela Universidade do Estado do Pará (Uepa).    Os resultados desse estudo serão apresentados, nesta quarta-feira (22), Dia Mundial da Água, no I Seminário do Laboratório de Qualidade da Água da Amazônia (Labágua), da Uepa, em funcionamento no Parque de Ciência e Tecnologia do Guamá. O tema da apresentação é "Saneamento e Qualidade Microbiológica das Águas Superficiais do Rio Guamá, em Belém do Pará", reunindo ainda a pesquisadora Danielle Salgado, que trabalhou a qualidade de água no município de Barcarena.    No Dia Mundial da Água, vale a pena não esquecer que esse bem responde por 71  da superfície terrestre do planeta, totalizando 1,4 bilhão de metros cúbicos. De toda a água disponível na Terra, 97,5  é água salgada e somente 2,5  da água disponível é doce.    VEJA MAIS                No Rio Guamá    Carla Renata Carneiro destaca que a constatação de valores elevados de coliformes termotolerantes no Rio Guamá "pode ser reflexo de problemas relacionados à precariedade do saneamento em Belém, principalmente em relação à coleta e tratamento de esgoto, pois o Rio Guamá é o corpo hídrico receptor; logo, é imprescindível políticas públicas voltadas ao saneamento na cidade, principalmente em relação à coleta e tratamento de esgoto".     Essa situação nas águas do rio tem reflexos na saúde da população, como doenças de veiculação hídrica e relacionadas à falta de saneamento, por exemplo, amebíase, giardíase, hepatite infecciosa A, leptospirose e dengue, segundo destaca a pesquisadora, autora dessa pesquisa de mestrado.                                                          "O alerta que faço em relação ao Dia Mundial da Água é de que a sociedade mude seu pensamento de que a água é um recurso natural infinito; a água é finita e precisa de maior atenção quanto aos seus usos e melhora na qualidade, principalmente quando se trata de consumo humano", ressalta Carla Renata.    A professora Hebe Morgane, coordenadora do Labágua da Uepa, salienta que o projeto Laboratório foi financiado pela Fundação Amazônia de Amparo a Estudos e Pesquisas (Fapespa) em 2021 e funciona no PCT Guamá, do Governo do Estado, e desde então contribui com as ações de ensino, pesquisa e extensão. Nesse sentido, atuam no Labágua alunos de graduação e pós-graduação, e a pesquisa na temática água é o carro-chefe do Laboratório, que presta serviços e análises relacionadas à qualidade de água, balneabilidade, potabilidade para a comunidade em geral.    Amazônia    A Amazônia, região que ocupa mais de 60  do território do Brail, tem um 162 mil quilômetros cúbicos subterrâneos de água, conhecido como Sistema Aquífero Grande Amazônia (Saga). E é dessa água que depende a vida na região, em especial, a cobertura florestal.
text_en: The surface waters of the Guamá River, which are used for various purposes, have high levels of thermotolerant coliforms, which are bacteria that indicate that the water has come into contact with fecal matter. Everything indicates that the damage to water quality is being caused by the high level of pollution that reaches the river. Data from the research show that the amount of thermotolerant coliforms exceeds that indicated by the Conama resolution, which would be up to 1,000 nmp/100ml; points on the Guamá River presented values ​​above the legal limit allowed, such as 12,098 nmp/100ml. This data was collected by Carla Renata Carneiro, a lawyer and graduate in Biology, master's and doctoral student at the State University of Pará (Uepa). The results of this study will be presented this Wednesday (22), World Water Day, at the 1st Seminar of the Amazon Water Quality Laboratory (Labágua), of Uepa, in operation at the Guamá Science and Technology Park. The themeThe theme of the presentation is "Sanitation and Microbiological Quality of Surface Waters of the Guamá River, in Belém do Pará", which also includes researcher Danielle Salgado, who worked on water quality in the city of Barcarena. On World Water Day, it is worth remembering that this resource accounts for 71% of the planet's land surface, totaling 1.4 billion cubic meters. Of all the water available on Earth, 97.5% is salt water and only 2.5% is fresh water. SEE MORE On the Guamá River Carla Renata Carneiro highlights that the finding of high levels of thermotolerant coliforms in the Guamá River "may be a reflection of problems related to the precariousness of sanitation in Belém, mainly in relation to sewage collection and treatment, since the Guamá River is the receiving water body; therefore, public policies aimed at sanitation in the city are essential, mainly in relation to sewage collection and treatment". This situation in the river's waters hasimpacts on the health of the population, such as waterborne diseases and those related to the lack of sanitation, for example, amoebiasis, giardiasis, infectious hepatitis A, leptospirosis and dengue, according to the researcher, author of this master's research. "The warning I make in relation to World Water Day is that society changes its thinking that water is an infinite natural resource; water is finite and needs greater attention regarding its uses and improvement in quality, especially when it comes to human consumption", emphasizes Carla Renata. Professor Hebe Morgane, coordinator of Labágua at Uepa, emphasizes that the Laboratory project was funded by the Amazon Foundation for the Support of Studies and Research (Fapespa) in 2021 and operates at the Guamá PCT, of the State Government, and since then has contributed to teaching, research and extension actions. In this sense, undergraduate and graduate students work at Labágua, and research on the themeWater is the flagship of the Laboratory, which provides services and analyses related to water quality, bathing suitability, and potability for the community in general. Amazon The Amazon, a region that occupies more than 60% of Brazil's territory, has 162 thousand cubic kilometers of underground water, known as the Greater Amazon Aquifer System (Saga). And it is on this water that life in the region depends, especially the forest cover.

text: Resumo São apresentados os dados coletados em um levantamento sobre a qualidade de água do rio Negro, nas proximidades da cidade de Manaus, Amazonas. Foram medidos alguns parâmetros físico químicos, tais como temperatura, pH, condutividade elétrica, transparência de Secchi e avaliadas as condições microbiológicas da quantidade de bactérias saprobiontes totais e coliformes totais, durante o ano de 1977. O trabalho foi realizado com coletas mensais, em nove locais ao longo do rio e em dois igarapés que margeiam a cidade, com amostragens em duas profundidades. Discute-se a importância dos resultados sob o ponto de vista sanitário e ressalta-se a capacidade de autopurificação do rio.   Summary This paper presents a survey of some aspects of Rio Negro water quality in the vicinity of Manaus, Amazonas, Brazil. Measurements of temperature. pH, electrical conductivity, light penetration (Secchi), saprophyte and total coliform bacteria, were carried out from January through December of 1977. The samples were collected at two depths at eleven places along the river and from two streams at the outskirts of the town. The results are discussed from a sanitary point of view and the autopurification capacity of the river is emphasized.    Texto disponível apenas em PDF
text_en: Abstract Data collected in a survey of the water quality of the Rio Negro, near the city of Manaus, Amazonas, are presented. Some physical and chemical parameters, such as temperature, pH, electrical conductivity, and Secchi transparency, were measured, and the microbiological conditions of the quantity of total saprobiotic bacteria and total coliforms were evaluated during the year 1977. The study was carried out with monthly collections at nine locations along the river and in two streams bordering the city, with sampling at two depths. The importance of the results from a health point of view is discussed and the self-purification capacity of the river is highlighted. Measurements of temperature. pH, electrical conductivity, light penetration (Secchi), saprophyte and total coliform bacteria, were carried out from January through December of 1977. title: SERGIPE, O “RIO DOS SIRIS” - Fernando José de Sousa

text: Com pouco menos de 22 mil km², Sergipe é o menor Estado do Brasil. Existem alguns municípios brasileiros com área maior que esse Estado – Altamira, no Pará, tem 159 mil km²; Corumbá, em Mato Grosso, tem 64 mil km² e Porto Velho, em Rondônia, tem 34 mil km², entre muitos outros. A população de Sergipe também é pequena – são aproximadamente 2,3 milhões de habitantes.     Com apenas 210 km de extensão, o rio Sergipe consegue a façanha de ser o mais importante do Estado. Metade da população de Sergipe depende das águas dessa bacia hidrográfica para o seu abastecimento e múltiplos usos na agricultura e indústrias, entre muitos outros. Como citado no título, o nome do rio vem do tupi siri ‘ype, que significa “rio dos siris”.     A história colonial de Sergipe remonta ao final do século XVI, quando o militar português Cristóvão de Barros atacou os indígenas tupinambás do cacique Serigy e do seu irmão Siriri, que dominavam as terras entre a foz dos rios Sergipe e Vaza Barris. Após vencer os indígenas, Cristóvão de Barros fundou uma vila na foz do rio Sergipe – São Cristóvão. Esse assentamento depois seria transferido para as margens do rio Poxim e, depois, para a região do rio Paramopama, um dos afluentes do rio Vaza Barris.     Por volta de 1699, teria surgido um pequeno povoado às margens do rio Sergipe – Santo Antônio de Aracaju. Essa pequena cidade só ganharia relevância em meados do século XIX, quando as lideranças políticas da Província decidiram transferir a capital para a região. Estruturada como uma cidade planejada, a moderna Aracaju foi inaugurada oficialmente em 1855. Uma reunião da Assembleia Legislativa da Província nesse mesmo ano oficializou a mudança da capital de São Cristóvão para Aracaju.     Um ponto que pesou bastante para essa decisão foi a grande embocadura da foz do rio Sergipe, que favorecia imensamente as atividades de operações portuárias. Apesar de bastante extenso, o litoral brasileiro carece de boas áreas para a construção de portos – a foz de grandes rios sempre foi uma das melhores alternativas para a instalação dessas infraestruturas. Desde então, a história do rio Sergipe e de Sergipe se confundem.     O rio Sergipe tem parte de suas nascentes na Serra Negra, em Pedro Alexandre na Bahia e parte na localidade conhecida como Lagoa das Areias, região que pertence a Monte Alegre de Sergipe. Ambas regiões ficam dentro dos domínios do Semiárido Nordestino. O rio atravessa todo o território do Estado de Sergipe no sentido Leste-Oeste até desaguar no Oceano Atlântico.     A bacia hidrográfica do rio Sergipe ocupa uma área total de pouco mais de 3,6 mil km², o que corresponde a quase 17  da superfície do Estado e onde são abrangidos 26 municípios, sendo que 8 deles ficam totalmente inseridos dentro da bacia hidrográfica. Mais de 1 milhão de sergipanos dependem diretamente das águas da bacia hidrográfica do rio Sergipe, o que permite colocar em perspectiva a sua importância.     De acordo com dados da SEPLANTEC – Secretaria de Estado do Planejamento e da Ciência e Tecnologia de Sergipe, cerca de 46  do território da bacia hidrográfica do rio Sergipe é ocupada por pastagens para a criação de animais e 18,5  por atividades agrícolas. As áreas florestais correspondem a apenas 5,1  do território e também há menção de “matas pouco densas” ocupando 22,5  do território.     Conforme comentamos na postagem anterior, quando falamos do sofrido rio Vaza Barris, Sergipe pode ser classificado com um dos Estados campeões em desmatamentos no Brasil. Originalmente, a Mata Atlântica, com seus mais diferentes subsistemas florestais, cobria aproximadamente 2/3 da superfície do Estado. Com os desmatamentos para abertura de campos para o plantio de cana, essa vegetação foi praticamente dizimada, restando pouco mais de 8  da sua cobertura original.     Nas áreas do Semiárido, os desmatamentos ocorreram em função da expansão da pecuária – grandes extensões de caatingais foram queimados para o aumento artificial das áreas de pastagens. Destruição de cobertura vegetal e recursos hídricos são duas coisas de não combinam nenhum pouco – a bacia hidrográfica apresenta atualmente uma série de problemas ambientais, grande parte deles decorrentes desses desmatamentos históricos.     A destruição de extensas áreas da Mata Atlântica e da vegetação do Semiárido resultou na diminuição dos caudais dos rios da bacia hidrográfica. O rio também sofre com o lançamento de esgotos sem tratamento, assoreamento, mineração, retirada de grandes volumes de água por sistemas de irrigação, despejos de resíduos sólidos, destruição de remanescentes florestais, entre outros problemas. A receita dessa tragédia ambiental é a mesma “aplicada” em muitos outros rios brasileiros.     De acordo com estimativas recentes, a bacia hidrográfica do rio Sergipe possui a capacidade de fornecer um volume diário de 180 mil m³ de água para todos os seus usuários, onde se inclui o abastecimento de populações humanas e animais, além dos usos na agricultura e na indústria. O problema é que a demanda atual se aproxima dos 440 mil m³/dia, onde perto de 66,5  do volume é necessário apenas para o consumo das populações humanas.     Para suprir o atual déficit de água na bacia hidrográfica do rio Sergipe vem sendo necessário a captação de água em outras fontes. Uma adutora transporta diariamente perto de 12 mil m³ a partir do rio São Francisco, água que é usada principalmente por indústrias. Também entram na conta grandes volumes de águas captados em rios próximos como o Poxim, Pitanga e Jacarecica, entre outros. Outra parte substancial dos recursos hídricos vem de poços artesianos, retirados principalmente de aquíferos como o Terra Dura.     Além de problemas ligados diretamente aos volumes de água, o rio Sergipe apresenta comprometimentos da sua qualidade físico-química. Análises feitas pelo ITPS – Instituto de Tecnologia e Pesquisas de Sergipe, vem encontrando grandes níveis de coliformes fecais nas águas, o que indica claramente o despejo de esgotos domésticos e efluentes de origem animal nas águas da bacia hidrográfica sem qualquer tipo de tratamento. Coliformes fecais são bactérias encontradas nos intestinos de animais de sangue quente como bois, cavalos e seres humanos, e presentes em grande quantidade nas respectivas fezes.     Um outro problema importante a ser considerado é a intrusão de águas salina na região do baixo curso do rio Sergipe. Nas regiões de foz dos rios junto ao mar existe um delicado equilíbrio entre os caudais de águas doces e as águas salinas. Sempre que um rio apresenta a diminuição dos seus caudais, a água salgada consegue invadir a calha do rio, deixando as águas salobras e impróprias para o consumo humano e para dessedentação animal, além dos usos na agricultura e na indústria.     Em 1978, quando já se notava o crescimento desse problema, foi construído um vertedor de concreto cortando o rio Poxim, afluente do rio Sergipe, onde é feita a captação de parte importante da água usada no abastecimento de Aracaju e cidades próximas. Essa obra foi executada justamente para impedir a propagação da salinidade das águas do baixo curso do rio Sergipe, algo que seria impensável em épocas passadas quando o rio “vendia saúde’.     A situação complicada do rio Sergipe se junta à de tantos outros rios importantes da faixa litorânea do Nordeste Brasileiro, onde a Mata Atlântica imperava num passado já bem distante. Felizmente, ainda existem fontes alternativas para a captação de água em Sergipe. A pergunta é – até quando essas fontes alternativas vão conseguir garantir a complementação do abastecimento da população?
text_en: With just under 22,000 km², Sergipe is the smallest state in Brazil. There are some Brazilian municipalities with an area larger than this state – Altamira, in Pará, has 159,000 km²; Corumbá, in Mato Grosso, has 64,000 km² and Porto Velho, in Rondônia, has 34,000 km², among many others. The population of Sergipe is also small – there are approximately 2.3 million inhabitants. At just 210 km long, the Sergipe River manages to be the most important in the state. Half of the population of Sergipe depends on the waters of this river basin for their supply and multiple uses in agriculture and industry, among many others. As mentioned in the title, the name of the river comes from the Tupi word siri ‘ype, which means “river of crabs”. Sergipe's colonial history dates back to the end of the 16th century, when the Portuguese soldier Cristóvão de Barros attacked the Tupinambá indigenous people of chief Serigy and his brother Siriri, who dominated the lands between the mouths of the Sergipe and Vaza Barris rivers. After defeating the indigenous people, Cristóvão de Barros founded a village at the mouth of the Sergipe river – São Cristóvão. This settlement would later be transferred to the banks of the Poxim river and then to the region of the Paramopama river, one of the tributaries of the Vaza Barris river. Around 1699, a small village emerged on the banks of the Sergipe river – Santo Antônio de Aracaju. This small city would only gain relevance in the mid-19th century, when the political leaders of the Province decided to transfer the capital to the region. Structured as a planned city, modern Aracaju was officially inaugurated in 1855. A meeting of the Provincial Legislative Assembly that same year made the change of the capital from São Cristóvão to Aracaju official. One factor that had a significant impact on this decision was the large mouth of the Sergipe River, which greatly favored port operations. Despite being quite extensive, the Brazilian coastline lacks good areas for the construction of ports – the mouths of large rivers have always been one of the best alternatives for the installation of these infrastructures. Since then, the history of the Sergipe River and Sergipe have been intertwined. The Sergipe River has part of its headwaters in Serra Negra, in Pedro Alexandre in Bahia, and part in the place known as Lagoa das Areias, a region that belongs to Monte Alegre de Sergipe. Both regions are within the domains of the Northeastern Semiarid Region. The river crosses the entire territory of the State of Sergipe in an East-West direction until it flows into the Atlantic Ocean. The Sergipe River basin covers a total area of ​​just over 3,600 km², which corresponds to almost 17% of the state's surface area and encompasses 26 municipalities, 8 of which are entirely within the basin. More than 1 million people from Sergipe depend directly on the waters of the Sergipe River basin, which puts its importance into perspective. According to data from SEPLANTEC – the State Secretariat for Planning, Science and Technology of Sergipe, around 46% of the Sergipe River basin is occupied by pastures for raising animals and 18.5% by agricultural activities. Forest areas correspond to only 5.1% of the territory and there is also mention of “sparse forests” occupying 22.5% of the territory. As we mentioned in the previous post, when we talked about the suffering Vaza Barris River, Sergipe can be classified as one of the states with the highest deforestation rates in Brazil. Originally, the Atlantic Forest, with its many different forest subsystems, covered approximately 2/3 of the state's surface. With deforestation to open fields for planting sugarcane, this vegetation was practically decimated, leaving just over 8% of its original coverage. In the semi-arid areas, deforestation occurred due to the expansion of livestock farming – large areas of caatinga were burned to artificially increase pasture areas.agens. Destruction of vegetation cover and water resources are two things that do not mix at all – the river basin currently presents a series of environmental problems, many of which are the result of historical deforestation. The destruction of large areas of the Atlantic Forest and the vegetation of the Semiarid region resulted in a decrease in the flow of the rivers in the river basin. The river also suffers from the release of untreated sewage, silting, mining, the withdrawal of large volumes of water by irrigation systems, the dumping of solid waste, the destruction of forest remnants, among other problems. The recipe for this environmental tragedy is the same “applied” to many other Brazilian rivers. According to recent estimates, the Sergipe River basin has the capacity to supply a daily volume of 180 thousand m³ of water to all its users, which includes the supply of human and animal populations, in addition to uses in agriculture and industry. The problem is that the current demand is close to 440 thousand m³/day, of which around 66.5% is needed only for human consumption. To meet the current water deficit in the Sergipe River basin, it has been necessary to collect water from other sources. A pipeline transports around 12 thousand m³ daily from the São Francisco River, water that is mainly used by industries. Large volumes of water are also taken from nearby rivers such as the Poxim, Pitanga and Jacarecica, among others. Another substantial part of the water resources comes from artesian wells, taken mainly from aquifers such as the Terra Dura. In addition to problems directly linked to water volumes, the Sergipe River has compromised physical and chemical quality. Analyses carried out by ITPS – Instituto de Tecnologia e Pesquisas de Sergipe, have found high levels of fecal coliforms in the water, which clearly indicates the dumping of domestic sewage and animal effluents into the waters of the river basin without any type of treatment. Fecal coliforms are bacteria found in the intestines of warm-blooded animals such as cattle, horses and humans, and are present in large quantities in their feces. Another important problem to be considered is the intrusion of saline water in the lower region of the Sergipe River. In the regions where rivers meet the sea, there is a delicate balance between the flow of fresh water and saline water. Whenever a river experiences a decrease in its flow, salt water can invade the riverbed, leaving the water brackish and unfit for human consumption and for drinking water for animals, in addition to being used in agriculture and industry. In 1978, when the problem was already growing, a concrete spillway was built across the Poxim River, a tributary of the Sergipe River, where a significant portion of the water used to supply Aracaju and nearby cities is collected. This work was carried out precisely to prevent the spread of salinity in the waters of the lower course of the Sergipe River, something that would have been unthinkable in times past when the river “sold health.” The complicated situation of the Sergipe River is in addition to that of many other important rivers along the coastal strip of Northeast Brazil, where the Atlantic Forest reigned in the distant past. Fortunately, there are still alternative sources for collecting water in Sergipe. The question is – how long will these alternative sources be able to guarantee the population’s supply?
