text: On s’entend, le Saint-Laurent n’est pas la mer des Caraïbes. Sa couleur tire sur le brun, parfois il pue et sa réputation est, disons-le, pas fameuse. Mais au-delà des apparences, la qualité de l’eau du fleuve est-elle assez bonne pour faire du surf, du SUP ou te baigner à Montréal sans craindre pour ta vie? Photo de couverture: Alexandra Côté-Durrer L’eau du fleuve Saint-Laurent: une eau de qualité? «Le fleuve a une eau de qualité, profitons-en!», s’écriait Valérie Plante avant de sauter à l’eau le 3 juillet 2018. Simple coup de pub ou déclaration du fond du cœur de la mairesse de Montréal? La mairesse de Montréal Valérie Plante se lance à l’eau lors du Grand Splash 2018. Photo: Patrick Sanfaçon, La PresseCe jour-là, la qualité de l’eau du fleuve était de 56 coliformes fécaux/100 ml, ce qui est nettement en dessous de la limite de 200 recommandée par le gouvernement du Québec pour faire une saucette sans danger. On est aussi bien loin du Gange, dont le score dépasserait de 3000 fois cette limite. Pourtant, 53  des Québécois n’oseraient pas s’y baigner. Pourquoi un tel dédain? À lire aussi: Combattre l’épidémie de plante zombie – myriophylle à épi – au Québec Petite histoire de la baignade dans le Saint-Laurent En 1950, il y avait une cinquantaine de plages dans la région de Montréal. En 1981, il n’en restait plus que 7. La croissance de la population urbaine, l’industrialisation et l’intensification des activités agricoles sur les rives ont grandement affecté la qualité de l’eau du fleuve. Pour te donner une idée, la ville de Montréal y déversait ses eaux usées sans même les traiter.   1/3Île Sainte-Hélène vers 1936. Photo: Musée McCord de Montréal/Harry Sutcliffe 2/3Club nautique de Cartierville vers 1910. Photo : Musée McCord de Montréal 3/3Île Sainte-Hélène vers 1938. Photo: Wikipédia      Petit à petit, la mauvaise qualité de l’eau a commencé à créer des problèmes de santé publique – comme des épidémies de gastro – et la plupart des plages ont été fermées. Après avoir réalisé l’ampleur du problème dans les années 1960, le gouvernement du Québec a mis beaucoup d’efforts dans le développement des solutions d’assainissement urbaines et industrielles. En 1970, la Régie des eaux du Québec a ordonné à la Communauté urbaine de Montréal de construire une usine d’épuration des eaux usées. La construction s’est terminée en 1986, et «la qualité des plans d’eau autour de l’île s’est grandement améliorée» depuis, selon la ville de Montréal.   La situation actuelle En 2019, la situation est encore loin d’être parfaite, surtout quand on pense au scandale du Flushgate, aux fameuses surverses ou au dernier bilan sur la qualité des plans d’eau de la ville de Montréal.  Les résultats d’échantillonnage obtenus l’été dernier démontrent que la qualité de l’eau s’est détériorée en 2018. Dans son rapport, la ville explique que les fortes pluies qui se sont abattuent sur Montréal sont l’un des facteurs qui ont contribué à la détérioration de la qualité de l’eau autour de la métropole. En 2018, seulement 50  des stations d’échantillonnage ont passé le test. Cela signifie que 50  des plans d’eau étaient problématiques lors d’un usage impliquant un contact direct avec l’eau, comme le SUP et le surf. En 2017, on parlait plutôt de 25 . Avec tout juste 50   de stations ayant obtenu l’approbation QUALO, c’est-à-dire qu’elles ont été propices aux usages de contact direct avec l’eau, l’année 2018 est nettement sous la moyenne de 60   obtenue depuis le début du programme en 1999. Au lac Saint-Louis, par exemple, l’année 2018 aura été l’une des moins bonnes depuis le début du programme, alors que seulement 11 des 25 stations, soit 44  , ont obtenu l’approbation QUALO. – Portrait de la qualité des plans d’eau à Montréal  Quand de fortes pluies s’abattent sur la ville, il arrive que le réseau de collecte n’arrive pas à fournir. Les eaux usées se retrouvent alors directement dans le Saint-Laurent, sans passer par la station d’épuration. Selon des données fournies par la ville, il y aurait en moyenne 24 épisodes de débordement par année, surtout en été. Heureusement, ce chiffre devrait réduire quand la ville aura complété la construction de cinq bassins de rétention en 2020. Photo: Scandale du Flushgate, crédit La PresseEn plus de ça, il y a le problème des raccordements inversés, qui toucherait pas moins du tiers du réseau de l’île de Montréal. Les contenus des toilettes des immeubles mal raccordés sont alors déversés dans le réseau d’égout pluvial à la place du réseau d’égout sanitaire et se retrouvent donc directement dans le fleuve. La ville de Montréal affirme être sur ce cas, mais il faudra attendre quelques années avant de trouver et de réparer toutes les installations fautives.  Tout est dans le timing Donc oui, on peut se baigner dans le fleuve, mais pas n’importe où et pas n’importe quand. Règle générale, tu devrais éviter le fleuve au moins 48h après de fortes averses, quand il y a de grosses chances que le réseau d’égouts ait débordé. Le contenu des toilettes de Montréal se retrouve alors dans notre beau fleuve, principalement dans le chenal de navigation et au nord de celui-ci. Tu ne veux pas prendre un bouillon cette journée-là!   1/3SUP Yoga dans le Fleuve Saint-Laurent à LaSalle. Photo: KSF 2/3 Balade de SUP dans le Fleuve Saint-Laurent à LaSalle. Photo: KSF 3/3Surf à Habitat 67 dans le Fleuve Saint-Laurent. Photo: KSF    « L’idée que l’eau du fleuve bordant l’île de Montréal ne soit pas de bonne qualité est trompeuse. » – Alain Saladzius, membre du Comité citoyen Montréal Baignade. Comment choisir le bon spot Le risque diminue lorsque le soleil brille depuis quelques jours. Pour avoir l’heure juste, tu peux consulter la carte interactive du réseau de suivi aquatique. La ville y publie les résultats d’analyses bactériologiques menées chaque semaine. Attention toutefois, les données sont publiées 24 à 48h après les analyses. La situation peut donc avoir changé entretemps.  Résultats Juin 2019Pour te jeter à l’eau l’esprit tranquille, mieux vaut combiner ces résultats avec ceux issus du Programme Environnement Plage, qui publie des données relatives aux plages de la région de Montréal, mais aussi d’ailleurs au Québec. Avec ça, tu pourras profiter du fleuve Saint-Laurent sans crainte, ou presque. Quels sont les risques? Le pire qui pourrait t’arriver en avalant un bouillon? Si tu t’es bien renseigné et que tu as tenu compte de la météo des derniers jours, le risque sera minime. C’est quand la qualité de l’eau est mauvaise que ta santé risque d’être affectée.  Selon le gouvernement du Québec, les problèmes de santé liés aux eaux de baignade contaminées sont majoritairement bénins et ne nécessitent pas de traitement. On parle surtout d’infections aux yeux, aux oreilles ou à la gorge et de troubles gastro-intestinaux. Mais avant de partir en peur, parles-en à nos amis de KSF, pour qui l’eau du fleuve n’a aucun secret. Après 23 ans de barbotage sur la vague à Guy, ils semblent encore jouir d’une santé du tonnerre! Le mot d’ordre : t’informer. Le deuxième : si tu tombes, ferme la bouche! Have fun!    Entrepreneur dévoué, excellent pédagogue et leader pour la protection de l’eau au Québec, c’est depuis les rives du Saint-Laurent qu’il vit sa passion au quotidien, avec sa petite famille. Il est aujourd’hui à la tête de Kayak Sans Frontières (KSF), entreprise qu’il a lui-même fondée en 1995 dans le but de faire profiter des eaux du fleuve au plus de gens possible. Tout d’abord destiné essentiellement au kayak, le centre a accueilli l’une des premières écoles de surf à Montréal en 2003 et a ajouté le stand up paddle (SUP) à sa liste de spécialités en 2008. text_en: Let’s be clear, the St. Lawrence is not the Caribbean Sea. Its colour is brown, it sometimes stinks and its reputation is, let’s face it, not great. But beyond appearances, is the quality of the river’s water good enough to surf, SUP or swim in Montreal without fearing for your life? Cover photo: Alexandra Côté-Durrer The water in the St. Lawrence River: quality water? “The river has quality water, let’s make the most of it!” exclaimed Valérie Plante before jumping into the water on July 3, 2018. Was it a simple publicity stunt or a heartfelt statement from the mayor of Montreal? Montreal Mayor Valérie Plante takes to the water during the 2018 Grand Splash. Photo: Patrick Sanfaçon, La PresseThat day, the water quality of the river was 56 fecal coliforms/100 ml, which is well below the limit of 200 recommended by the Quebec government for a safe dip. It is also a far cry from the Ganges, whose score is 3,000 times higher than this limit. However, 53% of Quebecers would not dare swim there. Why such disdain? Also read: Combating the zombie plant epidemic – Eurasian watermilfoil – in Quebec A brief history of swimming in the St. Lawrence In 1950, there were about fifty beaches in the Montreal region. By 1981, there were only 7 left. The growth of the urban population, industrialization and the intensification of agricultural activities on the banks greatly affected the quality of the river’s water. To give you an idea, the city of Montreal dumped its wastewater there without even treating it. 1/3Île Sainte-Hélène around 1936. Photo: McCord Museum of Montreal/Harry Sutcliffe 2/3Cartierville Boat Club around 1910. Photo: McCord Museum of Montreal 3/3Île Sainte-Hélène around 1938. Photo: Wikipedia Little by little, the poor quality of the water began to create public health problems – such as gastro epidemics – and most of the beaches were closed. After realizing the extent of the problem in the 1960s, the Quebec government put a lot of effort into developing urban and industrial sanitation solutions. In 1970, the Régie des eaux du Québec ordered the Communauté urbaine de Montréal to build a wastewater treatment plant. Construction was completed in 1986, and “the quality of the water bodies around the island has greatly improved” since then, according to the City of Montreal. The current situation In 2019, the situation is still far from perfect, especially when you think about the Flushgate scandal, the famous overflows or the latest report on the quality of the City of Montreal’s water bodies. Sampling results obtained last summer show that water quality deteriorated in 2018. In its report, the city explains that the heavy rains that fell on Montreal are one of the factors that contributed to the deterioration of water quality around the metropolis. In 2018, only 50 of the sampling stations passed the test. This means that 50 of the bodies of water were problematic for use involving direct contact with water, such as SUP and surfing. In 2017, the figure was more like 25. With just 50 stations having obtained QUALO approval, meaning that they were suitable for uses involving direct contact with water, 2018 was significantly below the average of 60 obtained since the program began in 1999. At Lac Saint-Louis, for example, 2018 was one of the worst years since the program began, with only 11 of the 25 stations, or 44, having obtained QUALO approval. – Portrait of the quality of bodies of water in Montreal When heavy rains hit the city, the collection network sometimes cannot supply. The wastewater then ends up directly in the St. Lawrence, without going through the stationtreatment plant. According to data provided by the city, there are an average of 24 overflow episodes per year, especially in the summer. Fortunately, this number should decrease once the city completes the construction of five retention basins in 2020. Photo: Flushgate scandal, credit La PresseIn addition to that, there is the problem of reverse connections, which affects no less than a third of the network on the island of Montreal. The contents of the toilets of poorly connected buildings are then discharged into the storm sewer system instead of the sanitary sewer system and therefore end up directly in the river. The city of Montreal claims to be on this case, but it will take a few years to find and repair all the faulty installations. Timing is everything So yes, you can swim in the river, but not just anywhere and not just anytime. As a general rule, you should avoid the river for at least 48 hours after heavy rain, when there is a good chance that the sewer system has overflowed. The contents of Montreal’s toilets then end up in our beautiful river, mainly in the navigation channel and north of it. You don’t want to get into trouble that day! 1/3SUP Yoga in the St. Lawrence River in LaSalle. Photo: KSF 2/3 SUP ride in the St. Lawrence River in LaSalle. Photo: KSF 3/3Surfing at Habitat 67 in the St. Lawrence River. Photo: KSF “The idea that the water in the river bordering the island of Montreal is not of good quality is misleading.” – Alain Saladzius, member of the Comité citoyen Montréal Baignade. How to choose the right spot The risk decreases when the sun has been shining for a few days. To get the real picture, you can consult the interactive map of the aquatic monitoring network. The city publishes the results of bacteriological analyses conducted each week. Be careful, however, the data is published 24 to 48 hours after the analyses. The situation may therefore have changed in the meantime. Results June 2019To jump into the water with peace of mind, it is best to combine these results with those from the Programme Environnement Plage, which publishes data on beaches in the Montreal region, but also elsewhere in Quebec. With this, you will be able to enjoy the St. Lawrence River without fear, or almost. What are the risks? The worst that could happen to you if you swallow a broth? If you have done your research and taken into account the weather of the last few days, the risk will be minimal. It is when the water quality is poor that your health is at risk. According to the Quebec government, health problems related to contaminated bathing water are mostly benign and do not require treatment. We are mainly talking about eye, ear or throat infections and gastrointestinal disorders. But before you run away in fear, talk to our friends at KSF, for whom the water of the river holds no secrets. After 23 years of splashing around on the wave at Guy, they still seem to be in great health! The watchword: inform yourself. The second: if you fall, shut your mouth! Have fun! A dedicated entrepreneur, excellent teacher and leader for the protection of water in Quebec, it is from the banks of the St. Lawrence that he lives his passion every day, with his small family. Today, he is at the head of Kayak Sans Frontières (KSF), a company that he himself founded in 1995 with the aim of making the waters of the river available to as many people as possible. Initially intended primarily for kayaking, the center welcomed one of the first surf schools in Montreal in 2003 and added stand-up paddle (SUP) to its list of specialties in 2008. Full episodes of the series are available in the series section. VIDEO VIDEO

title: Baignade: Peut-on faire confiance au fleuve Saint-Laurent?
snippet: 6 juill. 2015 — MONTRÉAL | Longtemps prisées par les habitants et les touristes, les plages publiques qui bordent le fleuve Saint-Laurent à Montréal ne sont ...

text: MONTRÉAL | Longtemps prisées par les habitants et les touristes, les plages publiques qui bordent le fleuve Saint-Laurent à Montréal ne sont plus ce qu’elles étaient autrefois.      Bon an, mal an, la réputation du fleuve quant à la baignade est bien amochée auprès des Montréalais. La qualité des eaux en inquiète plus d’un, et ce, même si de nombreuses initiatives ont été prises afin de lui redonner du lustre.     Joint au téléphone par Le Journal, Karel Mayrand, directeur général pour le Québec de la Fondation David Suzuki, reconnaît qu’il faut jouer de prudence.     «Oui, on peut se baigner, mais pas n’importe où. Il y a certains endroits, comme les plages à Cap Saint-Charles ou à Verdun, par exemple, où la qualité des eaux le permet. Toutefois, il y a des endroits trop pollués pour se risquer», admet-il.     Pour sa part, la mairesse de Rivière-des-Prairies-Pointe-aux-Trembles et responsable de l'eau à Montréal, Chantale Rouleau, abonde dans le même sens.     «De manière générale, la qualité de l’eau est assez bonne. Toutefois, il y a des moments, principalement lorsqu’il y a de fortes pluies, où elle est moins bonne.»                                                                                                                                          Photo d'archives, Agence QMI                                                                        Éradiquer le problème     Lors de journées de grandes pluies, le réseau d’égout de la ville atteint sa pleine capacité et cela entraîne un risque de surverse du trop-plein d’eaux pluviales et sanitaires dans le fleuve.        Selon les dires de Mme Rouleau, la volonté du maire de Montréal, Denis Coderre, est «extrêmement claire» et il y aura «des investissements importants» – autour de 4,6 milliards $ sur dix ans – afin de corriger la situation.     Dès cette année, il y aura la mise en place d’un programme de correction des raccordements inversés pour améliorer le diagnostic et le dépistage.     «Nous mettons aussi en place des bassins de rétention qui permettent de conserver les surplus d’eau lors des grandes pluies le temps qu’on puisse les redistribuer dans le système de conduite sous-terrain, assure-t-elle. Cela devrait alléger certains secteurs et quartiers résidentiels.»                                                                                                                                          Photo d'archives, Agence QMI                                                                        Ouvrir les portes du fleuve      Malgré l’amélioration des techniques d’assainissement des eaux usées ou encore la mise en place de règlementations plus strictes, la qualité des eaux n’est pas le seul et unique problème.     Plusieurs personnes déplorent un manque criant d’accès publics à l’eau, qui a été entraîné par la privatisation et l’industrialisation des berges et des rives qui ceinturent l’île de Montréal.     «Il faut rendre ça plus attrayant, souligne M. Mayrand. Créer des points d’accès, des plages et effectuer un travail de sensibilisation avec les gens pour leur dire que nous vivons sur une île.»     Au fil du temps, les habitants de la métropole ont tourné le dos au fleuve au profit du nombre grandissant de piscines publiques.     «Montréal est une île et on dirait que nous sommes les derniers à le savoir. Nous sommes constitués à 70   d’eau et 100   de cette eau provient du fleuve. Il coule dans nos veines. Il n’y a pas de frontières naturelles entre le fleuve et nous», reconnaît-il.                                                                                                                                          Photo d'archives, Agence QMI                                                                        Certification QUALO      Le Réseau de suivi du milieu aquatique (RSMA) de la Ville de Montréal a créé une carte interactive – disponible sur internet – qui permet d’effectuer un suivi accru de la qualité des cours d’eau à Montréal.     «On a mis en place depuis plusieurs années le système QUALO – un sceau qui certifie la qualité des eaux en rives pour la baignade», raconte la responsable de l’eau à Montréal.     Au total, ce sont 140 points d’échantillonnage des rives à Montréal qui sont passés au peigne fin afin de détecter le nombre de coliformes fécaux (bactéries) par 100 mL d’eau.      Plus du quart des sites sont certifiés QUALO.
text_en: MONTREAL | Long popular with locals and tourists, the public beaches along the St. Lawrence River in Montreal are no longer what they once were. Year after year, the river’s reputation for swimming has taken a hit among Montrealers. The quality of the water worries many, even though many initiatives have been taken to restore its luster. Reached by phone by Le Journal, Karel Mayrand, executive director for Quebec of the David Suzuki Foundation, acknowledges that caution is needed. “Yes, you can swim, but not just anywhere. There are some places, like the beaches at Cap Saint-Charles or Verdun, for example, where the water quality allows it. However, there are places that are too polluted to risk it,” he admits. For her part, the mayor of Rivière-des-Prairies-Pointe-aux-Trembles and responsible for water in Montreal, Chantale Rouleau, agrees. “Generally speaking, the water quality is quite good. However, there are times, mainly when there is heavy rain, when it is not as good.” Archive photo, Agence QMI Eradicating the problem During days of heavy rain, the city’s sewer system reaches its full capacity and this creates a risk of overflow of storm water and sanitary water into the river. According to Ms. Rouleau, the will of Montreal Mayor Denis Coderre is “extremely clear” and there will be “significant investments” – around $4.6 billion over ten years – to correct the situation. Starting this year, a program will be put in place to correct reverse connections to improve diagnosis and screening. “We are also setting up retention basins that allow us to retain excess water during heavy rains until we can redistribute it into the underground pipe system,” she assures. This should alleviate some sectors and residential neighbourhoods.” Archive photo, Agence QMI Opening the doors to the river Despite the improvement of wastewater treatment techniques and the implementation of stricter regulations, water quality is not the only problem. Many people deplore a glaring lack of public access to water, which has been caused by the privatization and industrialization of the banks and shores that surround the island of Montreal. “We need to make it more attractive,” emphasizes Mr. Mayrand. “Create access points, beaches and do awareness work with people to tell them that we live on an island.” Over time, the city’s residents have turned their backs on the river in favor of the growing number of public swimming pools. “Montreal is an island and it seems like we are the last to know it. We are made up of 70% water and 100% of that water comes from the river. It flows through our veins. There are no natural boundaries between the river and us,” he acknowledges. Archive photo, Agence QMI QUALO Certification The City of Montreal’s Aquatic Environment Monitoring Network (RSMA) has created an interactive map – available online – that allows for increased monitoring of the quality of waterways in Montreal.eal. “We have had the QUALO system in place for several years – a seal that certifies the quality of riverbank water for swimming,” says the person responsible for water in Montreal. In total, 140 sampling points on the banks of Montreal are combed through to detect the number of fecal coliforms (bacteria) per 100 mL of water. More than a quarter of the sites are QUALO certified.

title: La fierté des Québécois, le fleuve Saint-Laurent, va mal

trans_snippet: June 24, 2019 — coli spread in the river. The effects of wastewater discharges, particularly from the City of Montreal, are more persistent than expected...
text: De ses berges ou directement sur ses flots, les touristes d’ici et d’ailleurs admirent en cette saison estivale les étendues majestueuses du grand fleuve Saint-Laurent qui transperce le sud du Québec telle une flèche qui remonte vers la région des Grands Lacs au coeur du continent. L’été est aussi la période de l’année privilégiée par les scientifiques pour examiner le fleuve et mesurer les pesticides, les produits chimiques et tous les rejets d’eaux usées dans lesquels se mélangent les coliformes fécaux et les produits pharmaceutiques. Or, les effets de la pollution s’accentuent. Pas moins de 3 millions de Québécois boivent l’eau du Saint-Laurent. Au cours des 20 dernières années, la construction de plus de 600 stations d’épuration a permis de diminuer les rejets des municipalités de façon importante. Des problèmes persistent toutefois à certains endroits en raison des rejets de l’exploitation agricole ou de la contamination provenant des eaux usées non traitées.  François Guillemette – UQTR  L’une des analyses les plus poussées est celle réalisée par l’équipe du professeur François Guillemette, chercheur et professeur au Département de sciences de l’environnement de l’Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières (UQTR) qui a étudié pendant deux étés le fleuve Saint-Laurent entre sa source dans les Grands Lacs et Sainte-Anne-de-la-Pérade à proximité de l’estuaire, une distance de plus de 1000 km. Son premier constat est à quel point la bactérie E. coli s’est répandu dans le fleuve. Les effets des rejets d’eaux usées, particulièrement de la Ville de Montréal sont plus persistants, que prévu.  Crédit photo : Radio-Canada  FR_Reportage_1-20190613-WRF10Une nouvelle enquête scientifique en cours  Le professeur et cochef de mission, Gilbert Cabana Photo : Radio-Canada  Cet été, d’autres scientifiques comptent mesurer eux aussi les conditions du fleuve. Gilbert Cabana, du Département des sciences de l’environnement de l’UQTR, s’intéresse aux conséquences de la présence des résidus humains sur le fleuve Saint-Laurent. « Ce qui nous inquiète beaucoup, c’est que l’état du fleuve change très rapidement en ce moment », explique le professeur. Il explique que la bactérie E. coli a tendance par exemple à rester collée sur le bord du fleuve à proximité des endroits les plus visités par les touristes ou les baigneurs. Par conséquent, 44   de ces secteurs ne seraient pas plus propice à la baignade, alors que l’eau la plus pure se trouverait directement au centre de la voie navigable, en plein coeur du cours d’eau, là où circulent les grands navires.  Aide-mémoire… Le Saint-Laurent, fleuve gigantesque qui possède l’estuaire le plus large du monde, forme avec les Grands Lacs un réseau hydrographique qui s’étend sur 3790 km à l’intérieur de l’Amérique du Nord. Prenant sa source dans le lac Ontario, le fleuve est d’une longueur d’environ 1197 kilomètres et coule en direction nord-est jusqu’à Montréal, puis à Québec, où il va se jeter dans le golfe du Saint-Laurent. Le bassin hydrographique de ce fleuve occupe environ un million de kilomètres carrés, dont 505 000 kilomètres carrés se trouvent sur le territoire des États-Unis, et son débit moyen de près de 10 100 mètres cubes par seconde est le plus important du Canada. Sur le plan géologique, le Saint-Laurent est un fleuve jeune, dont le lit correspond à une brèche profonde dans l’écorce terrestre mise à découvert il y a quelque 10 000 ans lorsque les glaciers se sont retirés.    Une enquête internationale se mobilise Une autre équipe de l’Université Laval évalue pour sa part les impacts de l’activité humaine et des changements climatiques sur le Saint-Laurent. Ils effectuent leur recherche sur le Saint-Laurent de Montréal à Gaspé en passant par le golfe du Saint-Laurent. L’étude fait partie d’un effort multidisciplinaire international regroupant des chercheurs de cinq pays. L’équipe de l’Université Laval composée d’une trentaine de chercheurs et d’étudiants enquête sur l’impact de certaines combinaisons de facteur de stress comme le dragage, le transport maritime, le déversement de pétrole ou d’engrais. En tout, une trentaine de stresseurs sont pris en compte par ces chercheurs. L’équipe de chercheurs réalisera des travaux sur le terrain cet été. Une partie du travail a déjà été réalisée. On a développé une carte de tous les facteurs pour la partie estuaire et golfe du Saint-Laurent. Un site Internet sera mis en ligne et pourra être consulté sous peu. text_en: From its banks or directly on its waters, tourists from here and elsewhere admire this summer season the majestic expanses of the great St. Lawrence River that pierces southern Quebec like an arrow heading up toward the Great Lakes region in the heart of the continent. Summer is also the time of year preferred by scientists to examine the river and measure pesticides, chemicals and all wastewater discharges in which fecal coliforms and pharmaceutical products mix. However, the effects of pollution are increasing. No fewer than 3 million Quebecers drink water from the St. Lawrence. Over the past 20 years, the construction of more than 600 treatment plants has significantly reduced municipal discharges. However, problems persist in some places due to discharges from agricultural operations or contamination from untreated wastewater. François Guillemette – UQTR One of the most in-depth analyses is that carried out by the team of Professor François Guillemette, researcher and professor in the Department of Environmental Sciences at the Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières (UQTR), who studied the St. Lawrence River for two summers between its source in the Great Lakes and Sainte-Anne-de-la-Pérade near the estuary, a distance of more than 1,000 km. His first observation is the extent to which the E. coli bacteria has spread in the river. The effects of wastewater discharges, particularly from the City of Montreal, are more persistent than expected. Photo credit: Radio-Canada FR_Reportage_1-20190613-WRF10A new scientific investigation is underway Professor and co-leader of the mission, Gilbert Cabana Photo: Radio-Canada This summer, other scientists also plan to measure the conditions of the river. Gilbert Cabana, from the UQTR Department of Environmental Sciences, is interested in the consequences of the presence of human waste on the St. Lawrence River. “What worries us a lot is that the state of the river is changing very quickly at the moment,” explains the professor. He explains that the E. coli bacteria tends, for example, to remain stuck to the edge of the river near the places most visited by tourists or swimmers. Consequently, 44 of these areas would not be more suitable for swimming, while the purest water would be found directly in the centre of the waterway, in the heart of the waterway, where large ships travel. Reminder… The St. Lawrence, a gigantic river with the widest estuary in the world, forms with the Great Lakes a hydrographic network that extends over 3,790 km inland from North America. Rising from Lake Ontario, the river is approximately 1,197 kilometres long and flows northeast to Montreal and then to Quebec City, where it empties into the Gulf of St. Lawrence. The river’s watershed covers approximately one million square kilometres, 505,000 square kilometres of which are in the United States, and its average flow of nearly 10,100 cubic metres per second is the largest in Canada. Geologically speaking, the St. Lawrence is a young river, whose bed corresponds to a deep breach in the Earth’s crust that was exposed some 10,000 years ago when the glaciers retreated. An international investigation is being mobilized Another team from Université Laval is assessing the impacts of human activity and climate change on the St. Lawrence. They are conducting their research on the St. Lawrence from Montreal to Gaspé via the Gulf of St. Lawrence. The study is part of an international multidisciplinary effort involving researchers from five countries. The Université Laval team of about thirty researchers and students is investigating the impact ofcertain combinations of stress factors such as dredging, shipping, oil or fertilizer spills. In all, some thirty stressors are taken into account by these researchers. The research team will be carrying out field work this summer. Some of the work has already been done. A map of all the factors has been developed for the estuary and Gulf of St. Lawrence. A website will be put online and will be available for consultation shortly. text: Beograd je najveći zagađivač fekalnim vodama na celom toku Dunava, iz kog se na više od 30 mesta kanalizacija uliva ili direktno u ovu evropsku reku ili preko njene pritoke Save. Najveći kanalizacioni ispusti kreću od Mosta na Adi, gde se uliva Topčiderska reka, preko ispusta kod Gazele i na delu Savske promende u samom srcu Beograda na vodi, sve do Ade Huje i ušća Mirijevskog potoka. Kad se tome dodaju ispusti novobeogradskih fekalnih voda u Dunav, jasno je zašto je u prestonici šetnja pored reka često neprijatna, a kupanje i pecanje u njima se ne preporučuje.                          Topčiderska reka, koja je u toku kroz Dedinje i Rakovicu pretvorena u kolektor fekalnih voda i industrijskog zagađenja, završava u Čukaričkom rukavcu, poznatom po neprijatnom mirisu, plutajućem otpadu, pa čak i leševima uginulih riba. Ovaj rukavac nastavlja se na Savu, duž koje se dalje nižu kanalizacioni ispusti, od kojih se naveći nalazi ispod mosta Gazela, gde se koncentrišu fekalne vode sa jedne strane od Kumodraža i Voždovca, i sa druge od Velikog i Malog mokrog luga, preko Učiteljskog naselja i Crvenog krsta. Stručnjak za urbane vode i profesor na Imperijal koledžu dr Čedo Maksimović objašnjava za „Novu“ da Beograd ukupno ima više od 30 kanalizacionih ispusta.  Foto: Goran Srdanov/Nova.rsOtvor kolektora kod Gazele zbog visokog vodostaja Dunava trenutno nije vidljiv, a zbog građevinskih radova uz taj deo keja prilaz je nemoguć. To, međutim, ekipu lista „Nova“ nije lišilo prizora ispuštanja fekalnih voda u Savu, na oko 300 metara uzvodno, gde je tik uz jedan od splavova izbijala mutna voda od koje se širio oštar neprijatan miris. Gostiju na splavu, na sreću, u tom trenutku nije bilo, a smo nastavili šetnju nizvodno, ka centralnom delu Beograda na vodi prateći mutnu mrlju i neprijatan miris koji se naizmenično smanjivao i pojačavao.  Ispust u Beogradu na vodi, u produžetku Nemanjine ulice, pored restorana Savanova, u kasnim prepodnevnim satima takođe nije bio aktivan, pa su šetači i oni koji su sedeli na klupama sa poglednom na kanalizacione ispuste bili pošteđeni neprijatnosti koje ih čekaju kasnije u toku dana, a koje će do punog izražaja doći u toku leta, kad nivo reke opadne i otvori se nađu iznad vode.  Ubedljivo najgori prizor zatekli smo na Adi Huji, na mestu gde se u Dunav izlivaju fekalne vode koje Mirijevski potok skuplja kroz Mirijevo, Karaburmu i Rospi Ćupriju. Ovaj kanalizacioni ispust u formi malog rukavca sa vodom u boji blata, okružen je deponijom plastičnog otpada koja se sa kopna širi u reku, ka olupini obližnjeg broda. Na samo oko sto metara uzvodno, gde se miris koji izaziva mučninu polako gubi stoji pecaroš kome, kako kaže, pecanje olakšava to što je ispust nizvodno i zaklonjen iza drveta. Stručnjak za vode, docent za Fakultetu za ekonomiju i inženjerski menadžment u Novom Sadu dr Ratko Bajčetić kaže za list „Nova“ da je jedan od najvećih problema Beograda pretvaranje manjih vodotokova u fekalnu kanalizaciju, pri čemu su samo Topčiderska reka i Mirijevski potok ostali nezacevljeni, tj. otvoreni fekalni vodotokovi sa uništenim biodiverzitetom, koji predstavljaju ruglo i izvor neprijatnih mirisa. Na novobeogradskoj strani Dunava, na samom ušću Save, na koje puca pogled sa Kalemegdana, nalazi se glavni sanitarni ispust za Novi Beograd i Zemun, objašnjava profesor Čedo Maksimović. Uzvodno od tog mesta, uz kej, nalazi se crpna stanica Karađorđev trg, glavna za prepumpavanje sanitarne vode iz ovog dela grada u Dunav. Preko puta stanice, odmah uz restoran, jedriličarski klub i pristanište za čamce koji voze do Lida, nalazi se još jedan ispust. Beograđanka Lara, koju smo sreli u blizini, kaže da nikad ne sedi baš na tom delu keja, ali da vetar neprijatne mirise ume da odnese i do restorana uzvodno, koje posećuje. „Ovde ispuštaju kanalizaciju obično uveče, ali šta da rade, moraju negde, velika je to voda, ona sve odnese“, poručuje nam čovek koji sa tog mesta prevozi građane do plaže na Velikom ratnom ostrvu.   Foto: Goran Srdanov/Nova.rsDr Bajčetić objašnjava da to baš nije tako, da ni Dunav nije svemoćan. „Uz sanitarnu vodu u Dunav stižu koliformne bakterije, menja se PH vrednost, smanjuje količina kiseonika. Reka je živ organizam, složen biodiverzitet koji zavisi od ravnoteže, koji se na ovaj način narušava. Promene izazivaju stres kod rečnih vrsta, što je najveći uzrok njihovog smanjenja. Zbog toga u zagađenom delu vodotoka imamo manje ribe, ali i manje kvalitetnu ribu, u lošijem fizičkom stanju – objašnjava naš sagovornik i podvlači da je na početku cele ove priče čovek – koji prvo da zagadi a onda na kraju jede produkte svog zagađenja. Beograd traži rešenje u zastareloj tehnologiji Beograd ne bi imao problem zagađenih reka da, kao svi veći evropski gradovi na Dunavu, ima sistem za prečišćavanje otpadnih voda. Rešenje je Vlada Srbije najavila u okviru projekta „Čista Srbija“, koje je Maksimović kritikovao kao loše jer predviđa ugradnju zastarele, skupe i energetski neefikasne tehnologije koja bi mogla da donese više štete nego koristi.   Dunav do Smedereva ne stigne da se prečisti Merenja pokazuju da brojnost bakterija u Dunavu nizvodno od Zemuna značajno raste, gde doseže i preko 100.000 koliformnih bakterija i preko 15.000 fekalnih koliformnih bakterija u 100 mililitra vode, da bi do Smedereva ovaj broj polako padao na vrednosti od 15.000, odnosno 5.000, navodi dr Ratko Bajčetić i objašnjava: „Dunav do Smedereva ne stigne u potpunosti da se prečisti, onda Smederevo još malo doda fekalne vode, malo Kovin sa druge strane, nakon čega ide uspor od Đerdapske elektrane. Sve to se slaže jedno na drugo i tu je ceo biodiverzotet pod stresom.“  BONUS VIDEO Smeće u Savi ***Pratite nas i na društvenim mrežama: Facebook Twitter  Instagram
text_en: Belgrade is the biggest polluter of fecal waters along the entire Danube, from which in more than 30 places sewage flows either directly into this European river or through its tributary Sava. The largest sewage outlets start from the Bridge on Ada, where the Topčiderska river flows, through the outlet near Gazela and on the part of the Sava Promenade in the very heart of Belgrade on the water, all the way to Ada Huja and the mouth of the Mirijevsko potok. When you add to that the discharge of New Belgrade's sewage into the Danube, it is clear why walking along the rivers in the capital is often unpleasant, and swimming and fishing in them are not recommended.                          Topčiderska river, which in its course through Dedinje and Rakovica has been turned into a collector of fecal water and industrial pollution, ends in Čukarica creek, known for its unpleasant smell, floating waste, and even corpses of dead fish. This backwater continues to the Sava, along which there are sewer outlets, the largest of which is located under the Gazela bridge, where fecal waters are concentrated on one side from Kumodraž and Voždovac, and on the other from Veliki and Mali mokro lugo, via the Učići settlement and the Red Cross. Dr. Čedo Maksimović, expert in urban water and professor at the Imperial College, explains to "Nova" that Belgrade has more than 30 sewage outlets in total.  Photo: Goran Srdanov/Nova.rs The opening of the collector at Gazela is currently not visible due to the high water level of the Danube, and due to construction works along that part of the quay, access is impossible. This, however, did not deprive the team of the newspaper "Nova" of the sight of the discharge of fecal water into the Sava, about 300 meters upstream, where cloudy water was gushing out right next to one of the rafts, emitting a sharp unpleasant smell. Fortunately, there were no guests on the raft at that moment, and we continued our walk downstream, towards the central part of Belgrade on the water, following a cloudy spot and an unpleasant smell that alternately decreased and increased.  The outlet in Belgrade on the water, in the extension of Nemanjina Street, next to the Savanova restaurant, was also not active in the late morning hours, so walkers and those sitting on the benches with a view of the sewer outlets were spared the inconvenience that awaits them later in the day. and which will come to full expression during the summer, when the river level drops and opens up above the water.  We found the worst scene by far on Ada Huja, at the place where the sewage collected by Mirijevski potok flows into the Danube through Mirijevo, Karaburma and Rospa Ćuprija. This sewage outlet in the form of a small backwater with water the color of mud, is surrounded by a landfill of plastic waste that spreads from the land into the river, towards the wreck of a nearby ship. Only about a hundred meters upstream, where the nausea-inducing smell slowly fades, stands a fisherman who, he says, finds fishing easier because the outlet is downstream and hidden behind a tree. Dr. Ratko Bajčetić, a water expert and assistant professor at the Faculty of Economics and Engineering Management in Novi Sad, told the newspaper "Nova" that one of the biggest problems in Belgrade is the conversion of smaller watercourses into fecal sewage, with only the Topčiderska Reka and Mirijevski Potok remaining unsealed. i.e. open faecal waterways with destroyed biodiversity, which represent a mockery and a source of unpleasant odors. Professor Čedo Maksimović explains that on the New Belgrade side of the Danube, at the very mouth of the Sava, which can be seen from Kalemegdan, is the main sanitary outlet for New Belgrade and Zemun. Upstream from that place, next to the quay, there is the pumping station Karađorđev trg, the main one for pumping sanitary water from this part of the city into the Danube. Across from the station, right next to the restaurant, the sailing club and the pier for boats going to Lido, there is another outlet. Lara from Belgrade, whom we met nearby, says that she never sits exactly on that part of the quay, but that the wind can carry unpleasant smells to the restaurant upstream, which she frequents. "Here, they release sewage usually in the evening, but what can they do, they have to go somewhere, it's a big water, it carries everything away", tells us the man who transports citizens from that place to the beachese on the Great War Island.   Photo: Goran Srdanov/Nova.rs Dr. Bajčetić explains that this is not the case, that even the Danube is not omnipotent. "With the sanitary water, coliform bacteria arrive in the Danube, the PH value changes, the amount of oxygen decreases. A river is a living organism, a complex biodiversity that depends on balance, which is disturbed in this way. Changes cause stress to river species, which is the biggest cause of their decline. That is why in the polluted part of the watercourse we have less fish, but also less quality fish, in a worse physical condition - explains our interlocutor and underlines that at the beginning of this whole story is man - who first pollutes and then in the end eats the products of his pollution. Belgrade is looking for a solution in outdated technology Belgrade would not have the problem of polluted rivers if, like all major European cities on the Danube, it had a waste water purification system. The solution was announced by the Government of Serbia as part of the "Clean Serbia" project, which Maksimović criticized as bad because it foresees the installation of outdated, expensive and energy-inefficient technology that could do more harm than good.   The Danube does not reach Smederevo to be purified. Measurements show that the number of bacteria in the Danube downstream from Zemun increases significantly, where it reaches over 100,000 coliform bacteria and over 15,000 faecal coliform bacteria in 100 milliliters of water, until reaching Smederevo this number slowly drops to values ​​of 15,000, or 5,000, states Dr. Ratko Bajčetić and explains: "The Danube does not reach Smederevo to be completely purified, then Smederevo adds a little more fecal water, a little Kovin on the other side, after which it slows down from the Đerdap power plant. All of that stacks up on top of each other and the entire biodiversity is under stress." BONUS VIDEO Garbage in the Sava *** Follow us on social networks: Facebook Twitter Instagram

trans_snippet: 24. June 2015 - Rijeka Miljacka, say, is her spine of our Sarajevo. It is 35.9 kilometers long, and is created by merging Paljanske Miljacka and Mokranjska ...
text: Rijeka Miljacka, kažu, kičma je našeg Sarajeva. Duga je 35,9 kilometara, a nastaje nastaje spajanjem Paljanske Miljacke i Mokranjske Miljacke. Piše: Sanja Šabanadžović, Radiosarajevo.ba Glavno izvorište Paljanske Miljacke nalazi se na Ravnoj planini. Izvire iz više izdana koji uglavnom nastaju akumuliranjem površinske vode koja propada kroz pukotine krečnjačkog terena Ravne planine. Svi ovi izdani i vrela obrazuju Paljanku Miljacku koja na svom putu kupi vodu još nekoliko stalnih i povremenih izvora.  Mokranjska Miljacka izvire iz pećine u Kadinom selu kod Pala na 1135 metara nadmorske visine i duga je 20,5 kilometara. text: Željeznica, Bosna i Miljacka zagađene su i opasne po zdravlje kupača, zaključak je Zavoda za javno zdravstvo Kantona Sarajevo.  Ta je ustanova obavila ispitivanje tijekom juna na lokacijama Ilidža, Rimski most i Bentbaša, a onda i izdala upozorenje građanima da ne koriste ove rijeke za kupanje jer su vodotoci zagađeni.  Fekalije i smeće završe u rijeci Razlog zagađenju je što što ni najuži centar grada nema kompletno odvođenje otpadnih voda u kolektor, a također zagađenje potiče i od sanitarnih otpadnih voda (kanalizacije), od zagađenja nastalog istresanjem smeća uz vodotoke te nepostojanje kanalizacione mreže u seoskim i prigradskim naseljima. "Analizom rezultata mikrobioloških pokazatelja uzetih uzoraka vode iz rijeka Kantona Sarajevo, konstatujemo svježe i starije fekalno zagađenje kod ispitivanih rijeka. Uglavnom se pokazuje veliki broj Koliformnih bakterija identifikovanih kao Escherichia coli, Enterococcus spp", ističu u Zavodu.  Bakterije, virusi, paraziti... Bolesti kojima su izložene osobe koje koriste rijeke u rekreativne svrhe, potiču od patogenih mikroorganizama koji tu dolaze iz otpadnih voda i kanalizacije.  "Najčešći uzročnici oboljenja jesu izolovane koliformne bakterije, Ešerihija koli (Escherichia coli), i Streptokokus fekalis (Streptococcus faecalis), mada uzrok mogu biti i druge patogene bakterije, virusi, paraziti... Najčešće bolesti su one koje se prenose fekalno - oralnim putem, odnosno gastroenteritisi, hepatitis zatim konjuktivitisi, te neke druge virusne i parazitarne bolesti", upozoravaju.  Zahvaćeni organi i simptomi Organi koje zahvataju ove bolesti su probavni trakt, urogenitalni trakt, koža, oči, uši i nos, a simptomi mogu biti temperatura, povraćanje, proljev, peckanje i bol pri mokrenju, crvenilo i iritacija očiju, te promjene na koži.  Treba naglasiti da su ove bolesti opasne, te da kod imunokompromitirajućih osoba mogu uzrokovati ozbiljne posljedice po organizam. Osim mikrobioloških uzročnika, i povećane koncentracije hemijskih tvari prisutnih u vodi, takođe imaju vrlo štetno djelovanje na organizam. Foto: Pixabay/Icol

text: 2021年4月，中央第二生态环境保护督察组对铁岭市进行现场督察。督察发现，铁岭市凡河新区污水管网破损严重，污水处理厂建成近10年没能正常运行，大量生活污水长期直排，造成凡河水质严重恶化；部分污水渗漏进入地下水，导致凡河新区地下水严重超标；铁岭市委市政府及其有关部门思想认识不到位，长期不作为、慢作为，相关问题一直未得到有效解决。 　　一、基本情况  　　铁岭市凡河新区于2007年开始建设，规划占地面积45平方公里，目前建成区面积22平方公里，现有常住人口约13万，铁岭市委市政府坐落于该区域。凡河为辽河的一级支流，流经凡河新区后汇入辽河。凡河新区污水处理厂设计处理能力3万吨/日，2012年建成投运，主要负责收集处置凡河新区生活污水。 　　二、主要问题  　　（一）对督察反馈的生活污水直排问题长期漠视，整改工作不力。第一轮中央生态环境保护督察及“回头看”均指出，辽宁省存在辽河流域污水处理设施及配套管网建设改造滞后、生活污水直排、水质恶化等问题。但铁岭市在两次制定督察整改方案过程中，未将凡河新区生活污水大量直排、地下管网不配套、污水处理厂长期不正常运行、凡河水质恶化等问题纳入整改方案进行整改。第一轮中央生态环境保护督察中，有群众来信反映凡河新区生活污水直排等问题，但铁岭市未经认真调查即认定不属实。近年来，虽然铁岭市及其有关部门开始研究解决该问题，但一直未采取实质性举措，直至今年3月底督察进驻前，匆匆用9天时间就建成了1400米临时管线，将大部分直排生活污水接入污水处理厂。  图1　新建1400米临时管线 　　（二）大量生活污水长期直排，凡河新区地下水受到严重污染。督察发现，由于地下污水管网不配套等问题，铁岭市凡河新区大量生活污水经地下管网汇入黑龙江路雨排干渠，通过凡河新区雨水泵站强排进入凡河，每日直排量为2万余吨。现场督察发现，由于大量生活污水长期直排，凡河水质由排污口上游的Ⅲ类恶化为排污口下游的劣Ⅴ类。《铁岭凡河新城水文地质调查报告》指出，凡河新区地下水受到污水管线泄漏影响。监测数据显示，26个地下水监测点位的44个水样中，氨氮浓度、总大肠菌群、细菌总数最高分别超过地下水Ⅳ类标准0.9倍、91倍和26倍。  图2　大量生活污水直排凡河 　　（三）凡河新区污水处理厂长期无法正常运行,未发挥应有作用。铁岭凡河新区污水处理厂主要负责铁岭凡河新区生活污水的收集处置，由于大量生活污水直排和渗漏问题长期未解决，进入污水处理厂的生活污水水量和水质均不能满足运行要求，污水处理厂长期无法正常运行，处理能力长期闲置。督察组调阅凡河新区污水处理厂运行数据显示，自2012年污水处理厂投运以来，进水化学需氧量一般在50毫克/升左右（相当于污水处理厂达标排放水平），日进水量仅为7000吨左右，无法维持污水处理厂正常运转，污水处理厂从未排放过生活污泥，出水总磷长期超标，致使投资1.45亿元建设的治污设施近十年没有发挥环境效益。  图3　污水处理厂进水浓度低 　　三、原因分析  　　铁岭市委、市政府学习贯彻习近平生态文明思想不够深入，对凡河水环境污染问题长期漠视，推进解决缓慢。铁岭市凡河新区管委会环境主体责任落实明显缺位，不作为、慢作为，长期忽视生活污水直排、污水处理厂不正常运行、凡河水质和凡河新区地下水严重污染等问题，导致有关问题一直未得到有效解决。 　　督察组将进一步调查核实有关情况，并按要求做好后续督察工作。
text_en: In April 2021, the Second Central Ecological and Environmental Protection Inspection Team conducted an on-site inspection of Tieling City. The inspection found that the sewage pipe network in Fanhe New District, Tieling City was seriously damaged, and the sewage treatment plant had not been able to operate normally for nearly 10 years after its construction. A large amount of domestic sewage was directly discharged for a long time, causing the water quality of Fanhe River to deteriorate seriously; some sewage leaked into the groundwater, causing the groundwater in Fanhe New District to seriously exceed the standard; the Tieling Municipal Party Committee, Municipal Government and its relevant departments did not have adequate ideological awareness, and had been inactive and slow for a long time, and related problems had not been effectively solved. I. Basic Situation Construction of Fanhe New District, Tieling City, began in 2007. The planned area is 45 square kilometers. The current built-up area is 22 square kilometers. The current permanent population is about 130,000. The Tieling Municipal Party Committee and Municipal Government are located in this area. Fanhe River is a first-level tributary of Liaohe River. It flows through Fanhe New District and then merges into Liaohe River. The Fanhe New District Sewage Treatment Plant has a designed treatment capacity of 30,000 tons/day. It was completed and put into operation in 2012. It is mainly responsible for collecting and disposing of domestic sewage in Fanhe New District. 2. Main Problems (I) Long-term indifference to the direct discharge of domestic sewage reported by the inspection team and ineffective rectification work. The first round of central ecological and environmental protection inspections and the "review" pointed out that Liaoning Province had problems such as lagging construction and renovation of sewage treatment facilities and supporting pipe networks in the Liaohe River Basin, direct discharge of domestic sewage, and deteriorating water quality. However, in the process of formulating the inspection and rectification plan twice, Tieling City did not include the large-scale direct discharge of domestic sewage in Fanhe New District, the lack of supporting underground pipe networks, the long-term abnormal operation of the sewage treatment plant, and the deterioration of the water quality of Fanhe River in the rectification plan for rectification. During the first round of central ecological and environmental protection inspections, some people wrote to report problems such as direct discharge of domestic sewage in Fanhe New District, but Tieling City determined that it was not true without serious investigation. In recent years, although Tieling City and its relevant departments have begun to study and solve this problem, no substantive measures have been taken. Until the end of March this year, before the inspection team arrived, a 1,400-meter temporary pipeline was hastily built in 9 days to connect most of the direct discharge of domestic sewage to the sewage treatment plant. Figure 1 New 1,400-meter temporary pipeline (II) Due to the long-term direct discharge of a large amount of domestic sewage, the groundwater in Fanhe New District is seriously polluted. The inspection found that due to the lack of supporting underground sewage pipe network and other problems, a large amount of domestic sewage in Fanhe New District, Tieling City, was discharged into the Heilongjiang Road rainwater drainage canal through the underground pipe network, and then discharged into the Fanhe River through the Fanhe New District rainwater pump station, with a daily direct discharge of more than 20,000 tons. The on-site inspection found that due to the long-term direct discharge of a large amount of domestic sewage, the water quality of Fanhe River deteriorated from Class III upstream of the sewage outlet to Class V downstream of the sewage outlet. The "Tieling Fanhe New City Hydrogeological Survey Report" pointed out that the groundwater in Fanhe New District was affected by the leakage of sewage pipelines. Monitoring data showed that among the 44 water samples from 26 groundwater monitoring points, the highest ammonia nitrogen concentration, total coliform group, and total bacteria exceeded the groundwater Class IV standard by 0.9 times, 91 times, and 26 times, respectively. Figure 2 Large amounts of domestic sewage are directly discharged into the Fanhe River (III) The Fanhe New District Sewage Treatment Plant has been unable to operate normally for a long time and has not played its due role. The Tieling Fanhe New District Sewage Treatment Plant is mainly responsible for the collection and disposal of domestic sewage in the Tieling Fanhe New District. Due to the long-term failure to solve the problem of large amounts of domestic sewage being directly discharged and leakage, the amount and quality of domestic sewage entering the sewage treatment plant cannot meet the operating requirements. The sewage treatment plant has been unable to operate normally for a long time and its treatment capacity has been idle for a long time. The inspection team reviewed the operating data of the Fanhe New District Sewage Treatment Plant and found that since the sewage treatment plant was put into operation in 2012, the chemical oxygen demand of the influent has generally been around 50 mg/L (equivalent to the standard discharge level of the sewage treatment plant), and the daily influent volume is only about 7,000 tons, which is unable to maintain the normal operation of the sewage treatment plant. The sewage treatment plant has never discharged domestic sludge, and the total phosphorus in the effluent has long exceeded the standard, resulting in the pollution control facilities invested 145 million yuan in nearly ten years without any environmental benefits. Figure 3 Low influent concentration of sewage treatment plant 　　III. Cause Analysis 　　The Tieling Municipal Party Committee and Municipal Government have not studied and implemented Xi Jinping's ecological civilization thought deeply enough, and have long ignored the pollution of Fanhe River water environment, and have been slow to promote solutions. The Tieling City Fanhe New District Management Committee has obviously failed to implement the main environmental responsibility, and has been inactive and slow to act. It has long ignored the direct discharge of domestic sewage, the abnormal operation of sewage treatment plants, the serious pollution of Fanhe River water quality and Fanhe New District groundwater, resulting in the relevant problems not being effectively solved. 　　The inspection team will further investigate and verify the relevant situation, and do a good job in follow-up inspections as required.

text: Non uno, non due, ma ben tre campanelli di allarme sono suonati in poco più di un anno, tra il maggio del 2020 e l’agosto del 2021. Tre morie di pesci nel tratto urbano del Tevere per le quali l’Agenzia Regionale per la Protezione Ambientale non è riuscita a indicare del tutto le cause. Si parla di "bolle anossiche", cioè di condizioni di assenza di ossigeno, ma causate da che cosa? I monitoraggi nei periodi precedenti avevano già indicato le criticità a livello di inquinanti. Nei due anni precedenti, dei sei punti di monitoraggio solo due erano etichettabili come “buoni”, uno invece era “sufficiente”, gli altri tre “scarsi”. Dalle rilevazioni dell’ARPA eseguite dopo le morie di pesci emergevano alte concentrazioni di erbicidi e di Escherichia coli, un batterio che indica la presenza di feci. Lo stato di salute del fiume che Virgilio nell’Eneide chiama Genitor Urbis preoccupa una serie di associazioni locali che si occupano volontariamente di tutela dell’ambiente e che si sono riunite in Agenda Tevere con lo scopo di promuovere azioni di tutela del fiume. Tra queste c’è l’associazione A Sud che, assieme al Comitato Romano Acqua Pubblica (CRAP), ha deciso di realizzare una vera e propria campagna di monitoraggio della qualità dell’acqua del Tevere per un intero anno, da marzo 2021 a febbraio 2022 che ha chiamato RomaUp.   Giù al Tevere: un esempio di citizen science Il progetto di monitoraggio, lo raccontano gli stessi promotori nel rapporto, non aveva l’intenzione di sostituirsi all’ARPA Lazio. Ma è fuor di dubbio che i prelievi e le analisi che l’Agenzia riesce a effettuare sono limitati e non hanno per focus primario il tratto urbano del Tevere. La citizen science, cioè i progetti di raccolta dati scientifici con la partecipazione dei volontari e della società civile, non ha però solamente lo scopo di colmare un piccolo o grande vuoto conoscitivo sul fronte quantitativo, ma anche quello di diffondere la conoscenza degli strumenti e della situazione ambientale, fornendo allo stesso tempo una leva di potenziamento e amplificazione del ruolo della società alla cosa pubblica. In questo caso la gestione e la salute del Tevere, per il quale è stato anche siglato un “contratto di fiume”, uno strumento di programmazione volontaria previsto dalla Carta Nazionale dei Contratti di Fiume, per la promozione della riqualificazione ambientale e paesaggistica dei territori fluviali. Con l’aiuto di Bruna Gumiero, docente a contratto all’Università di Bologna esperta in ecologia fluviale e citizen science, A Sud e gli altri protagonisti del progetto hanno messo a punto un protocollo di monitoraggio che prevedeva prelievi mensili in otto punti del tratto urbano del Tevere.                                             Per ognuno dei campioni di acqua raccolti nei diversi punti si sono ricercati diversi indicatori di potenziale inquinamento. Sceglierli non è stato facile, come si può leggere nel rapporto finale del monitoraggio, perché durante il suo corso urbano il Tevere incontra diversi tipi di sorgenti di inquinamento. Alla fine, i parametri analizzati sono stati sette parametri “spia” di diversi tipi di inquinamento, dalla carenza di ossigeno all’eccesso di nutrienti provenienti dal dilavamento delle aree coltivate, fino all’elevata carica batterica dovuta alla presenza di feci.   Come sta il Tevere Per quanto riguarda pH e conducibilità, due parametri generali che servono a fare l’identikit del fiume, non hanno presentato particolari preoccupazioni. Non così per altri parametri, a cominciare dalla concentrazione di Escherichia coli.   E. coli La sua concentrazione è considerata dalla scienza un ottimo indicatore dell’inquinamento organico ed è uno dei sospettati per le morie di pesci che hanno innescato il monitoraggio. Come si può vedere dal grafico qui sotto, dal punto 2 (Ponte Salario) verso valle i valori sono stati quasi sempre elevati, ma sono soprattutto due punti a preoccupare.          Il punto di raccolta del Ponte Salario è poco a valle dell’immissione delle acque dell’Aniene nel Tevere. Mentre l’ultimo punto di monitoraggio, il punto 8, si trova immediatamente a valle del depuratore di Roma Sud.                      Ammonio Secondo la Direttiva Europea 2000/60/CE sulla qualità delle acque, la presenza di ammonio è un ottimo allarme per la carenza di ossigeno (anossia), che potrebbe essere una delle cause delle morie di pesci. La situazione per questo parametro è risultata critica per tutto il corso del fiume e per tutta la durata del monitoraggio. “Solo il 6  dei dati”, si legge nel rapporto, “è inferiore a 0,24 mg/l", cioè è inferiore ai livelli di riferimento per la bassa qualità delle acque. Tradotto: non va per niente bene.                         Qui sono necessarie delle spiegazioni sui dati riportati in tabella. Uno dei principi del monitoraggio portato avanti dal progetto era la scelta di usare strumenti di monitoraggio semplici da utilizzare ed economici. A Sud e le altre associazioni coinvolte hanno scelto, cioè, di privilegiare la facilità rispetto all’accuratezza. Questo significa che i dati sull’ammonio, per esempio, sono indicati come forchette di valori. Per la visualizzazione abbiamo però scelto di utilizzare dei valori intermedi (vedi spiegazione nella didascalia del grafico) senza che questo inficiasse particolarmente l'attendibilità generale dei dati: come si vede la stragrande maggioranze dei valori indicano acque di “qualità scarsa” o “qualità cattiva”. Si tratta dei parametri stabiliti dall’indice il Livello di Inquinamento espresso dai Macrodescrittori per lo stato ecologico (LIMeco), introdotto dal Decreto Ministeriale 260 dell’8 novembre 2010. Anche la media dei singoli punti di prelievo, per quanto riguarda l’ammonio, è sempre critica per tutto l’anno monitorato:                     Fosfati L'inquinamento da fosfati nelle acque superficiali è direttamente collegato agli scarichi di depurazione non trattati e ai fertilizzanti agricoli. A differenza di ammonio e E. coli non è presente nel LIMeco, ma assieme all’azoto è uno dei componenti dei fertilizzanti agricoli. A differenza dell’azoto, però, si sposta soprattutto per deflusso superficiale e dilavamento, finendo così non in profondità, ma nelle acque superficiali come quelle fluviali.                     Anche nel caso dei fosfati i dati raccolti dal progetto si presentano come forchetta, quindi con una certa incertezza. Ma, come ha sottolineato Bruna Gumiero nella sua relazione tecnica, guardare i valori medi è comunque interessante. Questi mostrano che per cinque stazioni su otto i valori non sono preoccupanti, ma nell’ultimo punto di raccolta, a valle del depuratore di Roma Sud, si sono registrati due picchi ad agosto e settembre. “In sintesi”, si legge nel rapporto, “i valori dei fosfati presentano concentrazioni proporzionalmente superiori ai nitrati e di conseguenza la sorgente potrebbe provenire dall’inquinamento puntiforme degli scarichi più che dal dilavamento dei campi”.   Il Tevere non sta bene… Nonostante la cautela espressa da Gumiero, in particolare per la necessità di provvedere a misurazioni più precise, dai dai dati raccolti dai volontari emergono chiaramente delle criticità per quanto riguarda la salute delle acque del Tevere. Come si legge nelle conclusioni del rapporto, “gli alti livelli di ammoniaca accompagnati ad alti valori di Escherichia coli nonché la sporadica presenza di pesticidi nelle acque indicano che il Tevere non gode di buona salute”. Secondo Gumiero, “un aspetto che è stato ben evidenziato e che necessita di ulteriore approfondimento, è quello dell’elevato contenuto di inquinamento organico di origine fecale”. Un altro aspetto interessante che emerge dai dati è la differenza dei parametri tra i diversi punti di raccolta dei campioni. “Guardando i risultati nella loro interezza”, leggiamo, “è come se il fiume Tevere arrivasse tutto sommato pulito in città e iniziasse a peggiorare una volta superata la confluenza con l’Aniene”. La situazione peggiora ulteriormente a valle del depuratore di Roma Sud.    …e neanche l’Aniene sembra essere in salute "È l’Aniene che inquina il Tevere” era una frase emersa durante il lavoro preparatorio del progetto di monitoraggio. I dati sembrano indicare che c’è qualcosa di vero ed è una considerazione che è confermata anche da altri progetti di monitoraggio, come per esempio il progetto Flumen portato avanti da Climate art project che ha confermato la presenza di nitrati nelle acque dell’affluente del Tevere. La situazione dell’Aniene, unita alle considerazioni sul peggioramento a valle del depuratore, hanno chiaramente indicato la strada per il prossimo futuro. Sì, perché il monitoraggio si sta tenendo anche per un secondo anno, con alcuni accorgimenti. Innanzitutto, laddove è stato possibile si è cercato di provvedere a un miglioramento della qualità del dato raccolto, grazie alla creazione di una maschera per smartphone sviluppata dal progetto in collaborazione con l’associazione OnData, che si occupa di dati e data journalism. Ma si è anche allargato il campo di indagine: coinvolgendo altre associazioni ambientali che si occupano di tutelare l’Aniene, proprio sull’affluente del Tevere sono raccolti i parametri di qualità delle acque per il secondo anno del monitoraggio partecipato. Perché, come sottolineano i soci e le socie di A Sud, fare citizen science non vuol dire solamente raccogliere i dati, ma costruire relazioni e reti per un miglior rapporto tra società e risorse naturali, come il Tevere e l’Aniene.
text_en: Not one, not two, but three alarm bells rang in just over a year, between May 2020 and August 2021. Three fish kills in the urban stretch of the Tiber for which the Regional Agency for Environmental Protection was unable to fully indicate the causes. We are talking about "anoxic bubbles", that is, conditions of absence of oxygen, but caused by what? Monitoring in previous periods had already indicated critical issues in terms of pollutants. In the previous two years, of the six monitoring points only two could be labeled as "good", one was "sufficient", the other three "poor". The ARPA surveys carried out after the fish kills revealed high concentrations of herbicides and Escherichia coli, a bacterium that indicates the presence of feces. The state of health of the river that Virgil in the Aeneid calls Genitor Urbis worries a series of local associations that voluntarily deal with environmental protection and that have come together in Agenda Tevere with the aim of promoting actions to protect the river. Among these is the association A Sud which, together with the Comitato Romano Acqua Pubblica (CRAP), has decided to carry out a real monitoring campaign of the quality of the Tiber water for an entire year, from March 2021 to February 2022, which it called RomaUp. Down the Tiber: an example of citizen science The monitoring project, as the promoters themselves say in the report, was not intended to replace ARPA Lazio. But there is no doubt that the samples and analyses that the Agency is able to carry out are limited and do not have the urban stretch of the Tiber as their primary focus. Citizen science, i.e. scientific data collection projects with the participation of volunteers and civil society, does not only have the aim of filling a small or large knowledge gap on the quantitative front, but also that of spreading knowledge of the tools and the environmental situation, providing at the same time a lever for strengthening and amplification of the role of society in public affairs. In this case, the management and health of the Tiber, for which a “river contract” was also signed, a voluntary programming tool provided for by the National Charter of River Contracts, for the promotion of environmental and landscape redevelopment of river territories. With the help of Bruna Gumiero, a contract professor at the University of Bologna and an expert in river ecology and citizen science, A Sud and the other protagonists of the project developed a monitoring protocol that included monthly sampling at eight points in the urban stretch of the Tiber. For each of the water samples collected at the different points, different indicators of potential pollution were sought. Choosing them was not easy, as can be read in the final monitoring report, because during its urban course the Tiber encounters different types of pollution sources. In the end, the parameters analyzed were seven "indicator" parameters of different types of pollution, from oxygen deficiency to excess nutrients from the runoff of cultivated areas, to the high bacterial load due to the presence of feces. How is the Tiber As regards pH and conductivity, two general parameters that serve to create an identikit of the river, they did not present particular concerns. This was not the case for other parameters, starting with the concentration of Escherichia coli. E. coli Its concentration is considered by science to be an excellent indicator of organic pollution and is one of the suspects for the fish kills that triggered the monitoring. As can be seen from the graph below, from point 2 (Ponte Salario) downstream the values ​​were almost always high, but there are two points in particular that are worrying. The Ponte Salario collection point is slightly higher.downstream of the Aniene waters entering the Tiber. While the last monitoring point, point 8, is located immediately downstream of the Roma Sud purification plant. Ammonium According to the European Directive 2000/60/CE on water quality, the presence of ammonium is an excellent alarm for oxygen deficiency (anoxia), which could be one of the causes of fish deaths. The situation for this parameter was critical along the entire course of the river and for the entire duration of the monitoring. “Only 6 of the data,” the report states, “is lower than 0.24 mg/l", that is, it is lower than the reference levels for low water quality. In other words: it is not good at all. Here, some explanations are needed about the data reported in the table. One of the principles of the monitoring carried out by the project was the choice to use monitoring tools that were easy to use and cheap. A Sud and the other associations involved chose, that is, to favour ease over accuracy. This means that the data on ammonium, for example, are indicated as ranges of values. However, for the visualization, we chose to use intermediate values ​​(see explanation in the caption of the graph) without this particularly affecting the general reliability of the data: as can be seen, the vast majority of the values ​​indicate water of “poor quality” or “bad quality”. These are the parameters established by the Pollution Level index expressed by the Macrodescriptors for the ecological state (LIMeco), introduced by Ministerial Decree 260 of 8 November 2010. average of the individual sampling points, as regards ammonium, is always critical for the entire monitored year: Phosphates Phosphate pollution in surface waters is directly linked to untreated sewage discharges and agricultural fertilizers. Unlike ammonium and E. coli, it is not present in LIMeco, but together with nitrogen it is one of the components of agricultural fertilizers. Unlike nitrogen, however, it moves mainly through surface runoff and leaching, thus ending up not in depth, but in surface waters such as rivers. Even in the case of phosphates, the data collected by the project are presented as a range, therefore with a certain uncertainty. But, as Bruna Gumiero underlined in her technical report, looking at the average values ​​is still interesting. These show that for five out of eight stations the values ​​are not worrying, but in the last collection point, downstream of the Roma Sud purification plant, two peaks were recorded in August and September. “In summary,” the report states, “the phosphate values ​​have concentrations proportionally higher than nitrates and consequently the source could come from point pollution from wastewater rather than from field runoff.” The Tiber is not well… Despite the caution expressed by Gumiero, in particular for the need to provide more precise measurements, the data collected by the volunteers clearly show critical issues regarding the health of the Tiber’s waters. As stated in the conclusions of the report, “the high levels of ammonia accompanied by high values ​​of Escherichia coli as well as the sporadic presence of pesticides in the waters indicate that the Tiber is not in good health.” According to Gumiero, “an aspect that has been well highlighted and that requires further investigation is the high content of organic pollution of fecal origin.” Another interesting aspect that emerges from the data is the difference in parameters between the different sample collection points. “Looking at the results as a whole,” we read, “it is as if the Tiber River arrived in the city relatively clean and began to deteriorate once it passed the confluence with the Aniene.” The situationand it gets worse downstream of the Rome South purifier. …and the Aniene doesn’t seem to be healthy either “It’s the Aniene that pollutes the Tiber” was a phrase that emerged during the preparatory work of the monitoring project. The data seem to indicate that there is some truth to it and it is a consideration that is also confirmed by other monitoring projects, such as the Flumen project carried out by Climate art project which confirmed the presence of nitrates in the waters of the Tiber tributary. The situation of the Aniene, combined with the considerations on the worsening downstream of the purifier, have clearly indicated the path for the near future. Yes, because the monitoring is also being carried out for a second year, with some adjustments. First of all, where it was possible, an attempt was made to improve the quality of the data collected, thanks to the creation of a smartphone mask developed by the project in collaboration with the OnData association, which deals with data and data journalism. But the field of investigation has also expanded: by involving other environmental associations that deal with protecting the Aniene, the water quality parameters for the second year of participatory monitoring are collected on the Tiber tributary. Because, as the members of A Sud underline, doing citizen science does not only mean collecting data, but building relationships and networks for a better relationship between society and natural resources, such as the Tiber and the Aniene.
