In the territory of Porto Alegre alone, 27 hydrographic sub-basins can be delimited, composed mainly of streams and creeks, such as Arroio Dilúvio (MENEGAT et al., 2006MENEGAT, R.; PORTO, M.L.; CARRARO, C.C.; FERNANDES, L.A.A. (Coords.). (2006) Environmental Atlas of Porto Alegre. 3rd ed. Porto Alegre: Editora da UFRGS . 228 p.). Lake Guaíba has two-dimensional flow dynamics, controlled by fluctuations in the level of Laguna dos Patos and by the direction and intensity of the winds (MENEGAT et al., 2006MENEGAT, R.; PORTO, M.L.; CARRARO, C.C.; FERNANDES, L.A.A. (Coords.). (2006) Atlas Ambiental de Porto Alegre. 3rd ed. Porto Alegre: Editora da UFRGS . 228 p.). In the Ponta do Gasômetro region, the water flow can vary, on the same day, both in the South and North directions, which can cause the waters to be dammed. With this water regime, a large part of the water from the Guaíba is retained in the reservoir for a long period of time (MENEGAT et al., 2006MENEGAT, R.; PORTO, M.L.; CARRARO, C.C.; FERNANDES, L.A.A. (Coords.). (2006) Environmental Atlas of Porto Alegre. 3rd ed. Porto Alegre: Editora da UFRGS . 228 p.; MENEGAT & CARRARO, 2009MENEGAT, R.; CARRARO, C.C. (2009) Manual to know why the Guaíba is a lake: Integrated analysis of geology, geomorphology, hydrography, stratigraphy and history of science. Porto Alegre: Armazém Digital. 108 p.), which generates less circulation of water mass and, consequently, less dilution of pollutants. According to Laybauer and Bidone (2001LAYBAUER, L.; BIDONE, E.D. (2001) Caracterização textural dos sedimentos de fundo do Lago Guaíba (sul do Brasil) e sua importância em diagnósticos Ambientales. With the metropolitan region on its shores, Lake Guaíba has multiple uses, such as a water supply source, effluent dilution, transportation and navigation, fishing, tourism, leisure, among others. These uses have changed over time, with lake pollution acting as a limiting factor for some activities. THE HISTORICAL, ECONOMIC AND CULTURAL RELATIONSHIP WITH THE REGION Public supply and the origins of pollution In the first half of theIn the 19th century, the main form of access for Porto Alegre residents to drinking water was through public fountains and springs (and a few private ones) in the city center. However, these sources did not meet the population's demand, and water was traded (by the so-called “pipeiros” or “aguadeiros”), in addition to direct collection from the Guaíba, especially by the most disadvantaged population (RÜCKERT, 2013RÜCKERT, F.Q. (2013) O problema das águas poluidas na cidade de Porto Alegre (1853-1928). Diálogos, v. 17, n. 3, p. 1145-1172. dx.doi.org/10.4025/dialogos.v17i3.763 dx.doi.org/10.4025/dialogos.v17i3... ). The increase in population and, consequently, in the demand for drinking water led, still in the Brazilian imperial period, to the creation of the Porto-Alegrense Hydraulic Company (1861), which collected water from the source of the “Riacho do Sabão” (current Arroio Dilúvio). Later, during the republican period, the Companhia Hydraulica Guahybense (1891) was founded, with water collection from Guaíba (RÜCKERT, 2013RÜCKERT, F.Q. (2013) The problem of polluted water in the city of Porto Alegre (1853-1928). It is noteworthy that currently the Arroio Dilúvio runs for more than 15 km in areas of high population density, becoming one of the most polluted streams in Porto Alegre - comparable to the Tietê River in São Paulo - and having at its mouth one of the main entry points for organic and metal pollution into Lake Guaíba. Access to treated water was considered a symbol of modernization and civility, and was recommended by health authorities (RÜCKERT, 2013RÜCKERT, F.Q. (2013) The problem of polluted waters in the city of Porto Alegre (1853-1928). Diálogos, v. 17, n. 3, p. 1145-1172. dx.doi.org/10.4025/dialogos.v17i3.763 dx.doi.org/10.4025/dialogos.v17i3... ). However, at the beginning of the 20th century, with the increase in complaints about water quality and the strong competition between companies in the “water business”, Hydraulica Guahybense was taken over (RÜCKERT, 2013RÜCKERT, F.Q. (2013) The problem of polluted waters in the city of Porto Alegre (1853-1928). During the 19th century, a large part of the people of Porto Alegre directly consumed water from the same lake that received their waste,without any treatment, since the “cubes” (or “cabungos”) - containers placed under the seats of toilets and toilets - were thrown (through piers) into the Guaíba as a way of compensating the Municipal Intendancy for the lack of sewage collection. Aiming to meet the growing demand for “materials” and eliminate the initial pollution, at the end of the 19th century the cubes began to be transported by steam trains that ran along a railroad towards the South Zone of the city, taking the waste away from the central areas (GUIMARAENS, 2015GUIMARAENS, R. (2015) Águas do Guaíba. Porto Alegre: Libretos. 216 p., p. 86). In 1878, encouraged by the City Council, actions were taken to remove the “cubes” from Lake Guaíba; however, the releases did not cease after these operations, and the “unpleasant odors and scenes” persisted, in addition to organic contamination in the lake. The cubes were initially launched at “Ponta da Cadeia” (Gasômetro), later (until 1890) at “Ponta do Dionísio” - current area of ​​the Clube Veleiros do Sul, in the Assunção neighborhood - and, after that period, at “Ponta do Melo” (or “do Asseio”), where the “Estaleiro Só” operated, in the Cristal neighborhood (RÜCKERT, 2013RÜCKERT, F.Q. (2013) The problem of polluted waters in the city of Porto Alegre (1853-1928). Diálogos, v. 17, n. 3, p. 1145-1172. dx.doi.org/10.4025/dialogos.v17i3.763 dx.doi.org/10.4025/dialogos.v17i3... ). According to Rückert (2013RÜCKERT, F.Q. (2013) The problem of polluted waters in the city of Porto Alegre (1853-1928). Diálogos, v. 17, n. 3, p. 1145-1172. dx.doi.org/10.4025/dialogos.v17i3.763 dx.doi.org/10.4025/dialogos.v17i3... ), the pollution of Lake Guaíba in the 19th century and early 20th century occurred mainly due to the dumping of human waste (“cubes”), washing of clothes on the beaches and surrounding areas (including the Santa Casa de Misericórdia), lack of sanitary inspection in slaughterhouses and on ships in the ports, and proximity to the Public Jail (located next to the Gasometer, which gave rise to the name “Ponta da Cadeia”). At the same time, according to Prestes (2008PRESTES, A.J.D. (2008) Porto Alegre em tempo de praia: a cidade e as praias do Guaíba entre os anos 1940 e o início dos anos 1970. Revista Historiar, v. 2, 25 p.), the pollution of Guaíba follows the pattern of coastal cities, in which water bodies were commonly seen, until the mid-19th century, as a natural destination for their waste. The worldwide cholera epidemics of 1855 and 1885 alerted the authorities about the water consumed by the population, but the practice of dumping water in the Guaíba was old and was incorporated into the daily life of Porto Alegre society (RÜCKERT, 2013RÜCKERT, F.Q. (2013) O problema das águas poluidas na cidade de Porto Alegre (1853-1928). Diálogos, v. 17, n. 3, p. 1145-1172. dx.doi.org/10.4025/dialogos.v17i3.763 dx.doi.org/10.4025/dialogos.v17i3... ). The construction of the sewage system took years of discussion, including the Proclamation of the Republic, starting only in 1907 and being completed in 1912. However, these works did not stop the dumping of “cubes” into the Guaíba, and the lake ended up becoming the final destination of the sewage system (RÜCKERT, 2013RÜCKERT, F.Q. The historical degradation of Guaíba Lake The pollution of Guaíba Lake was already observed during the 19th century, by the population and the government, due to environmental factors such as the color and odor of the waters, gradually gaining importance on the government's agenda and in the local press (RÜCKERT, 2013RÜCKERT, F.Q. (2013) O problema das águas pproduced in the city of Porto Alegre (1853-1928). Diálogos, v. 17, n. 3, p. 1145-1172. dx.doi.org/10.4025/dialogos.v17i3.763 dx.doi.org/10.4025/dialogos.v17i3... ). Despite the notorious environmental damage, degradation continued over the decades. According to Prestes (2008PRESTES, A.J.D. (2008) Porto Alegre in beach time: the city and the beaches of Guaíba between the 1940s and the beginning of the 1970s. Revista Historiar, v. 2, 25 p.; 2014PRESTES, A.J.D. (2014) The pollution of Guaíba and its beaches in Porto Alegre from the 1960s onwards. In: PEREIRA, E.M.; RÜCKERT, F.Q.; MACHADO, N.G. (Orgs.). Environmental history of Rio Grande do Sul. Lajeado: Editora da Univates. 221 p.), the process was a consequence of the intense population growth of Porto Alegre and the metropolitan region, especially accelerated between the 1940s and 1970s, when it went from 272,000 to 903,000 inhabitants. The historical degradation of local water resources was not exclusive to Porto Alegre. Among the tributaries of Lake Guaíba, the Rio dos Sinos stands out for its high pollution, originating from the colonization of the region. According to Figueiredo et al. (2010FIGUEIREDO, J.A.S.; DRUMM, E.; RODRIGUES, M.A.S.; SPILKI, F.R. (2010) The Rio dos Sinos watershed: an economic and social space and its interface with environmental status. In the mid-20th century, the installation of leather and footwear factories in the São Leopoldo and Novo Hamburgo region stimulated rapid and unplanned growth of urban areas, negatively affecting the river basin. The environmental impacts caused by industrial development have economic and cultural links with the population, and according to Figueiredo et al. (2010FIGUEIREDO, J.A.S.; DRUMM, E.; RODRIGUES, M.A.S.; SPILKI, F.R. (2010) The Rio dos Sinos watershed: an economic and social space and its interface with environmental status. At the beginning of the 20th century, systematic and articulated urban transformations took place with the aim of modernizing the structures inherited from the colonial period in Brazilian metropolises. In Porto Alegre, this remodeling of public spaces occurred through landfills in Lake Guaíba (Rua da Praia, Praia de Belas, Beira Rio and others), similar to those carried out in coastal cities, with the expansion of territories, between the end of the 19th century and the beginning of the 20th century (BOHRER, 2002BOHRER, M.D. (2002) O Aterro Praia e Belas e o Aterro do Flamengo. In: RABENO, R. (Org.). Horizonte Metropolitano: a gestão territorial urbana na região metropolitana de Porto Alegre. Porto Alegre: Metroplan. 256 p.). The largest landfill in Porto Alegre, on the former Praia de Belas (a bathing area for the population in the past), was conceived in the 1930s and completed between the 1950s and 1970s. The landfill covers over 200 hectares, occupied by the Brazilian Navy and Maurício Sirotsky Sobrinho (Harmonia) parks and by administrative centers (PRESTES, 2008PRESTES, A.J.D. Porto Alegre: Editora da Universidade/UFRGS . 228 p.). Thus, increases in the lake's level have been frequent throughout history, with the highest flood in 1941, when the level reached 4.75 m (with an average of 1 m). Porto Alegre: Metroplan. 256 p., p. 154), “with the need for the containment dike, from the 1950s onwards, the potential of the waterfront was detached from the existing city, which began to be equated with the paradigm of the modern city”. Travelers' view of Lake Guaíba Until the 19th century, Lake Guaíba was the main access route to Porto Alegre and the region, entering from the ocean, passing through Laguna dos Patos and arriving at the capital, and also making it possible to continue traveling to the interior of the state via the Jacuí River and other tributaries. Some travelers recorded their impressions in travel diaries. The French botanist Auguste de Saint-Hilaire (1779-1853), in his diary Viagem ao Rio Grande do Sul (SAINT-HILAIRE, 2002), written in 1820-21 and originally published in 1887, described Guaíba as a “lagoon originating from navigable rivers and numerous tributaries”, forming a large basin. Saint-Hilaire also described the ports, the vessels and their relationship with communication with the sea and the interior of the state. However, the lack of sanitation and the beginning of pollution in Lake Guaíba were also described by the traveler: “the banks of the lagoon are cluttered with filth”; “the inhabitants only drink water from the lake and, continually, one sees black people filling their jugs in the same place where others have just washed their dirtiest vessels” (SAINT-HILAIRE, 2002SAINT-HILAIRE, A. (2002) Viagem ao Rio Grande do Sul (1820-1821). Brasília: Senado Federal, Conselho Editorial. 578 p. (Coleção O Brasil Visto por Estrangeiros).). Another French naturalist, Arsène Isabelle (1807-1888), also recorded his observations during a visit to Porto Alegre in 1834 - at the time “a very new city”, with “around 12 to 15 thousand inhabitants” (ISABELLE, 2006ISABELLE, A. (2006) Viagem ao Rio da Prata e ao Rio Grande do Sul (1833-1834). Brasília: Senado Federal, Conselho Editorial. v. 61. 314 p.). In her reports, Isabelle describes Lake Guaíba: “Five rivers, which bring the tribute of their fertile waters and meet there to form Rio Grande do Sul” (ISABELLE, 2006ISABELLE, A. (2006) Viagem ao Rio da Prata e ao Rio Grande do Sul (1833-1834). Brasília: Senado Federal, Conselho Editorial. v. 61. 314 p.). According to Isabelle, Guaíba was described as a “five-fingered hand”, formed by the rivers Jacuí (the thumb), Caí, Sinos, Gravataí and “Riacho” (old name of Arroio Dilúvio) - this vision would have originated the name of the neighboring municipality, Viamão. The naturalist also describes the Jacuí Delta and the “cove covered in ships” (national and foreign), in an economy heavily dependent on the Guaíba (ISABELLE, 2006ISABELLE, A. (2006) Viagem ao Rio da Prata e ao Rio Grande do Sul (1833-1834). Brasília: Senado Federal, Conselho Editorial. v. 61. 314 p.). In the travel diary of Dom Gastão de Orléans (Count d’Eu) - who accompanied Emperor Dom Pedro II, in 1865, during the Paraguayan Waruai (1864-1870) -, the prince also describes Lake Guaíba, praising its beauty and importance: “The presidential palace occupies the top of the city; the view from there is splendid. The waters of the lake stretch out on three sides, since the city is on a promontory. To the southeast, in the direction from which we came, the lake expands to the horizon” (CONDE D’EU, 1936CONDE D’EU. (1936) Viagem militar ao Rio Grande do Sul (august to November 1865). São Paulo: Companhia Editora Nacional. 290 p., p. 35). The perception of environmental degradation in Lake Guaíba Disguised by the beauty of its shoreline, pollution in Guaíba progressed along with the population. The various uses of its waters were increasingly reduced to indirect ones, and the saying that “Porto Alegre turned its back on the Guaíba” gradually became popular. According to Bohrer (2002BOHRER, M.D. (2002) O Aterro Praia e Belas e o Aterro do Flamengo. In: RABENO, R. (Org.). Horizonte Metropolitano: a gestão territorial urbana na região metropolitana de Porto Alegre. Porto Alegre: Metroplan. 256 p.), “the people of Porto Alegre have never established a permanent relationship with the Guaíba on a city scale”. The beaches of Guaíba were once heavily frequented by bathers, especially between the 1940s and 1970s, and were systematically abandoned as pollution of the lake increased since the 1950s. Despite the strong historical, cultural and emotional connection with the lake, the acceptance of pollution and the “loss of beaches” was seen by the population, in general, as something natural, an “inevitable consequence of the growth of underdeveloped economies” (PRESTES, 2008PRESTES, A.J.D. (2008) Porto Alegre em tempo de praia: a cidade e as praias do Guaíba entre os anos 1940 e o início dos anos 1970. Revista Historiar, v. 2, 25 p.), a similar fact to what occurred in the Bacia do Rio dos Sinos (FIGUEIREDO et al., 2010FIGUEIREDO, J.A.S.; DRUMM, E.; RODRIGUES, BUT.; SPILKI, F.R. (2010) The Rio dos Sinos watershed: an economic and social space and its interface with environmental status. Brazilian Journal of Biology, v. 70, n. 4, p. 1131-1136.  dx.doi.org/10.1590/S1519-69842010000600001 dx.doi.org/10.1590/S1519-69842010... ).         The history of the degradation of Lake Guaíba is reported in local news coverage, which, during the 1950s and early 1960s, positively portrayed the “image of nautical clubs, sailboats and speedboats in Guaíba” and, at the end of the 1960s, made the approach to domestic and industrial pollution more common (PRESTES, 2008PRESTES, A.J.D. (2008) Porto Alegre em tempo de praia: a cidade e as praias do Guaíba entre os anos 1940 e o início dos anos 1970. Revista Historiar, v. 2, 25 p.). In the late 1950s, Henrique Luiz Roessler (2005ROESSLER, H.L. (2005) O Rio Grande do Sul e a Ecologia. 2nd ed. Porto Alegre: Governo do Estado do Rio Grande do Sul / SEMA / FEPAM. 219 p.) criticized, in newspaper articles, water pollution and the discharge of untreated effluents into the Guaíba Lake Basin. Roessler was one of the first representatives from Rio Grande do Sul of the growing global environmental movement. At that time, in response to environmental criticism, factories located near Lake Guaíba claimed that the installation of effluent treatment systems would have “prohibitive” costs (PRESTES, 2008PRESTES, A.J.D. (2008) Porto Alegre em tempo de praia: a cidade e as praias do Guaíba entre os anos 1940 e o início dos anos 1970. Revista Historiar, v. 2, 25 p.). In 1958, journalist Kleber Borges de Assis also reported on the situation of Lake Guaíba in a series in the newspaper Correio do Povo, compiled in the book O Rio Que Não é Rio (ASSIS, 1960ASSIS, K.B. (1960) O Rio que não é Rio. Porto Alegre: Livraria do Globo. 130 p.). Assis states that “The Guaíba has ‘picturesque places’ on its banks, as well as beautiful beaches where, in the summer, part of the population of Porto Alegre takes refuge”, having social and economic importance, with functions of transport, supplyment and recreation. According to Assis (1960ASSIS, K.B. (1960) O Rio que não é Rio. Porto Alegre: Livraria do Globo. 130 p.), in the 19th and 20th centuries there were rowing, sailing, swimming, diving and water polo competitions on Lake Guaíba. However, by the end of the 1950s, environmental changes in the lake were already noticeable, mainly related to rice crops in the region (due to their negative effects on fishing activity), coliforms (from domestic sewage) and “industrial waste” (not only directly, but also in the rivers that make up the basin and flow into the lake). In the early 1960s, Rocha Freitas, a sanitation engineer and professor at the Institute of Hydraulic Research (IPH/UFRGS), also warned about the quality of the Guaíba in his thesis The fate of Porto Alegre's sewage systems in the face of the pollution of the Guaíba (FREITAS, 1962). In this work, Freitas (1962) discusses water quality and concludes that “Porto Alegre depends on the Guaíba for its drinking water supply” and that “there is no other source capable of supporting it in the future”, “therefore, it is essential to preserve it”. At the same time (1961), the Municipal Department of Water and Sewage (DMAE) of Porto Alegre was created (DMAE, 2015). During the growing global environmental pressure between the 1960s and 1970s, combined with the rebirth of the labor movement and the historical context of the political reopening of the military regime, several environmental activists emerged. Among them, agronomist José Lutzenberger is one of the most remembered names in Brazilian environmentalism and an icon in the fight against pollution in the Guaíba, especially in the case of Borregaard, a cellulose industry that began its operations in 1972, in the municipality of Guaíba (RS). For many years, this industry was a popular symbol of pollution in the region (due to its effluents and, mainly, the odor of its atmospheric emissions) and was also a catalyst for the environmental movement in Rio Grande do Sul (PRESTES, 2008). With the pollution of Lake Guaíba becoming increasingly evident, in 1973, many of the lake's beaches were closed off and warning signs were placed about the quality of the water. In 1975, DMAE completed the installation of a subfluvial emissary to discharge most of Porto Alegre's untreated sewage into the Guaíba navigation channel, from Ponta da Cadeia (Gasômetro), despite opposition from many environmentalists and experts to the project (PRESTES, 2014PRESTES, A.J.D. (2014) Pollution of the Guaíba and its beaches in Porto Alegre from the 1960s. In: PEREIRA, E.M.; RÜCKERT, F.Q.; MACHADO, N.G. (Orgs.). Environmental history of Rio Grande do Sul. Lajeado: Editora da Univates. 221 p.). Between 1979 and 1985, with the implementation of the Southern Petrochemical Complex, in Triunfo (RS), metropolitan region of Porto Alegre, there was constant concern among environmentalists about the chemical pollution of the Guaíba. As a result, government programs aimed at cleaning up the lake emerged, such as the “Rio Guaíba” (1981), “Guaíba Vive” (1989) and “Pró-Guaíba” (1989) projects, which were added to the quality monitoring by DMAE, which had already been taking place since the 1970s (GUIMARAENS, 2015GUIMARAENS, R. (2015) Águas do Guaíba. Porto Alegre: Libretos. 216 p.). Considering the environmental reality and the importance of Guaíba for the metropolitan population of Porto Alegre, scientific studies specifically about the lake are still scarce. FINAL CONSIDERATIONS Despite the great importance of Guaíba Lake for the metropolitan region of Porto Alegre, there is a historical neglect of its quality. The lake is polluted, with public awareness of this reality and limitations on the direct use of its waters. Several depollution programs have been and are being implemented, with favorable future prospects; however, the results are not yet visible with respect to environmental quality, and more studies should be directed at this area. The quality of Lake Guaíba is directly linked to the quality of life of the populations that directly or indirectly use its waters, and its revitalization should be a public priority for the region. Furthermore, due to the use and occupation of the areas of the Guaíba Hydrographic Basin, the sustainable use of natural resources is essential, as well as the reduction of organic discharges and industrial and urban waste into the water bodies adjacent to the basin.

text: ARTÍCULOS ORIGINALES     Avaliação  da qualidade da água do Rio dos Sinos (Brasil) por meio do teste de micronúcleos  em Cyprinus  carpio e de  análises físico-químicas e microbiológicas      Evaluation  of water quality of the Sinos River (Brazil) by micronucleus test   in Cyprinus  carpio and  physicochemical and microbiological analysis            Santos  de Souza Mateus¹*, Zimmermann Prado Rodrigues Gabriela¹, Dalzochio Thaís¹,   Goldoni  Angélica², Ressel Simões Leonardo Airton¹, Gehlen Günther¹, Basso da Silva  Luciano²      1Universidade  Feevale. Campus 2. Instituto de Ciências da Saúde. Laboratório de Histologia  Comparada. Endereço: Rodovia RS-   239, km 2755, CEP 93352-000, Novo  Hamburgo, RS, Brasil. ²Universidade Feevale. Campus 2. Instituto de Ciências da  Saúde.   Laboratório  de Citogenética Animal. Endereço: Rodovia RS-239, km 2755, CEP  93352-000, Novo Hamburgo, RS, Brasil. *mateussouza@feevale.br      Recibido: 9 de noviembre de 2015Aceptado: 9 de septiembre de 2016 Resumo.      O Rio dos Sinos está localizado na região sul do  Brasil, possui aproximadamente 190   km de extensão e fornece água   para  atividades agrícolas, industriais e para o consumo de mais de um milhão de  habitantes. Este rio é considerado um dos mais   poluídos  do Brasil e, portanto, estudos para avaliar a qualidade da água ao longo de sua  extensão são necessários. O teste de   micronúcleos  em eritrócitos de peixes tem sido utilizado com sucesso para detectar a  presença de poluentes mutagênicos nos   ambientes  aquáticos. O objetivo do presente estudo foi avaliar a qualidade da água do Rio  dos Sinos por meio do teste de micronúcleos   em Cyprinus carpio bem como  de análises físico-químicas e microbiológicas. Foram coletadas amostras de água  nos   trechos  superior (Caraá), médio (Parobé) e inferior (Novo Hamburgo) do Rio dos Sinos em  dezembro de 2013. As amostras foram   transportadas  para o laboratório para análise de 14 parâmetros de qualidade da água bem como  para a exposição de espécimes   de C. carpio por 72h em aquários. Não foram  verificadas diferenças significativas na frequência de micronúcleos e  anormalidades   nucleares  nos grupos expostos a água do rio em comparação ao grupo controle. Apenas um  parâmetro de qualidade da água   foi  observado em desacordo com a legislação no trecho superior do rio, enquanto que  nos trechos médio e inferior foram seis e   cinco  parâmetros, respectivamente. Os resultados demonstram que o Rio dos Sinos  apresenta redução da qualidade da água ao   longo de  sua extensão e indicam ausência de potencial genotóxico no período amostrado.      Palavras-chave: Rio dos  Sinos; Biomarcadores; Qualidade da água; Cyprinus carpio.        Abstract.      The Sinos River  is located in South of Brazil, it has about 190 km of extension and  provides water for agricultural and   industrial  activities, and for consumption of more than one million inhabitants. This  river is considered one of the most polluted   rivers  in Brazil;  therefore, studies aiming to evaluate the water quality along its course are  necessary. The micronucleus test in   fish  erythrocytes has been successful used to detect mutagenic pollutants in the  aquatic environment. The objective of this study   was to  evaluate the water quality of the Sinos   River by the micronucleus  test in Cyprinus  carpio, as  well as physicochemical and   microbiological  analyses. Water samples were collected in the upper (Caraá municipality),  middle (Parobé municipality) and lower   (Novo Hamburgo municipality) sections of the Sinos River,  in December 2013. The samples were transported to the laboratory   for  analysis of 14 water quality parameters and for exposure of C. carpio for 72  hours in aquaria. Significant differences in micronucleus   and  nuclear abnormalities frequencies were not found between the control and the  exposed groups. Only one parameter   of water  quality exceeded the limit of the legislation in the upper section of the  river, while in the middle and lower sections, six   and five  parameters, respectively. These results show that the Sinos River  presents a reduction in water quality along its extension   and  indicates the absence of genotoxic potential in the sampled period.      Keywords: Sinos  river; Biomarkers; Water quality; Cyprinus carpio. Introdução      O Rio  dos Sinos, localizado na região nordeste   do Rio  Grande do Sul, é considerado um   dos  principais rios do estado, concentrando   na área  de sua bacia hidrográfica significativa   percentagem  da população, além de um gran de parque industrial e turístico (Comitesinos   2000).  Ao longo de sua extensão, de aproximadamente   190 km, fornece água para  atividades   agrícolas,  industriais e para consumo   humano,  sendo também utilizado como meio de diluição de efluentes de esgoto doméstico,   efluentes  industriais e dejetos de origem rural   (Bieger et al. 2010).      Os  impactos provocados pelas atividades antrópicas   contribuem  para a redução da qualidade   da água  do Rio dos Sinos. Monitoramentos   de  parâmetros físico-químicos da água   realizados  ao longo do rio indicam que essa   redução  ocorre principalmente no seu trecho   inferior,  próximo a grandes centros urbanos,   nos  quais há maior densidade populacional e   industrial  (Blume et al. 2010).  De acordo com   o órgão  estadual de meio ambiente (SEMA   2014),  diversos pontos ao longo do rio foram   avaliados  nas classes III e IV de qualidade   de água  conforme classificação estabelecida   pela  resolução brasileira CONAMA 357/2005   (Brasil  2005), na qual a classe I representa a   melhor  qualidade e a classe IV a pior.      Além do  monitoramento de parâmetros físicoquímicos,   diversos  estudos propondo a utilização   de  bioindicadores como ferramentas   complementares  na avaliação da qualidade   das  águas do rio têm sido realizados (Schulz   e  Martins-Júnior 2001; Rechenmacher et al.   2010;  Scalon et al. 2010;  Nunes et al. 2011;   Scalon et al. 2013;  Weber et al. 2013;  Bergamaschi   et al. 2015;  Bianchi et al. 2015).  Tais   estudos  são importantes para que a análise   dos  impactos provocados pelas atividades   antrópicas  seja mais ampla, visto que proporcionam   a  possibilidade de revelar o potencial   tóxico  da água aos organismos vivos. Peixes   são  bastante utilizados como bioindicadores   de  ambientes aquáticos, tanto em estudos in   situ, devido  a sua grande disponibilidade e   importante  papel na cadeia trófica (Oost et al.   2003),  como em laboratório, devido à facilidade   de manutenção  e exposição (Al-Sabti e   Metcalfe  1995).     O teste  de micronúcleos e anormalidades nucleares   em  eritrócitos de peixes é uma ferramenta   muito  utilizada para análise da genotoxicidade   da água  devido a sua simplicidade   e  rapidez de análise (Bolognesi e Hayashi   2011).  Os micronúcleos são fragmentos cromossômicos   ou  cromossomos inteiros não   inseridos  no núcleo celular durante o processo   de  divisão (Al-Sabti e Metcalfe 1995). As   anormalidades  nucleares são deformações na   morfologia  do núcleo, as quais também são   consideradas  indicadoras de efeitos genotóxicos (Çavas e  Ergene-Gözükara 2005).      A  espécie Cyprinus  carpio (Linnaeus,  1758)   da  família Cyprinidae, conhecida popularmente   como  carpa comum, é muito utilizada   em  pisciculturas no Brasil. É originária da Europa   Oriental  e da Ásia Ocidental e foi uma   das  primeiras espécies a serem cultivadas em   aquicultura.  Atualmente seu cultivo ocorre em   todos os  continentes devido a sua rusticidade   e  facilidade de criação (Querol et al. 2005). A   espécie  já foi utilizada com sucesso em estudos   de avaliação de genotoxicidade (Buschini   et al.  2004; Gustavino et al. 2005; Canistro   et al.  2012; García-Medina et al. 2013). Nesse   contexto,  o objetivo do presente estudo foi   avaliar  a qualidade da água do Rio dos Sinos   por meio  do teste de micronúcleos em C. carpio   bem como  de análises físico-químicas e   microbiológicas.      Material e  métodos         Área de  estudo      A Bacia  Hidrográfica do Rio dos Sinos está localizada   a  nordeste do estado do Rio Grande   do Sul,  entre as coordenadas geográficas de   29° 20' a 30° 10' de latitude Sul e 50° 15' a 51°   20' de longitude Oeste. Possui  área de aproximadamente   3.800  km², abrangendo, parcial ou   totalmente,  32 municípios e uma população estimada   em  1.249.000 habitantes (SEMA 2010).   O principal  curso de água da bacia e que dá   nome a  mesma é divido em três trechos: superior,   com 25 km de extensão,  caracterizado   por alta  declividade do fundo e rápido fluxo   das  águas; médio, que se estende por 125   km   e cuja  altitude varia de 60 m  a 5 m em  declividade   média;  inferior, com aproximadamente   50 km de extensão, no qual a  declividade é   suave e  o fluxo das águas é lento (Comitesinos   2000).      O trecho  superior apresenta baixa densidade   populacional  e atividades econômicas predominantemente   rurais. No  trecho médio e principalmente   no  trecho inferior há grandes concentrações   populacionais  e industriais, sendo   que  afluentes do Rio dos Sinos drenam grandes   centros  urbanos como Novo Hamburgo e   São  Leopoldo. O trecho inferior da bacia é o   que está  exposto a maior pressão antrópica   e nele  está instalada a maior base industrial   do  estado do Rio Grande do sul (Figueiredo   et al. 2010).       Coleta de  águas superficiais      No mês  de dezembro de 2013 foram realizadas   as  coletas de amostras de águas superficiais   em três  pontos do Rio dos Sinos, localizados   nos  municípios de Caraá (29° 45'  44.4" S  / 50° 19' 39.8" W), Parobé (29° 41' 10.7"   S/ 50° 51' 03.4"W) e Novo Hamburgo (29°  44'   12.5" S/ 51° 05' 29.1" W), representando os   três  trechos do rio, superior, médio e inferior,   respectivamente  (Figura 1). As  amostras foram   conduzidas  ao laboratório, sendo os seguintes   parâmetros  analisados de acordo com o   Standard  Methods for the Examination of Water   and  Wastewater (APHA 1998): demanda   bioquímica  de oxigênio (DBO), demanda química   de  oxigênio (DQO), fósforo total, nitrogênio   amoniacal,  sólidos suspensos, coliformes   totais e  termotolerantes, alumínio, chumbo,   cobre,  cromo total, ferro, níquel e zinco. Procedimento  experimental        O  protocolo experimental do presente trabalho   foi  aprovado pela Comissão de Ética   no Uso  de Animais da Universidade Feevale   (protocolo  n.02.13022). Espécimes de C. carpio   (n=40)  foram adquiridos de um piscicultor   local e  aclimatados por sete dias em água da   torneira  declorificada com aeração constante,   em sala  com temperatura controlada (22±1ºC)   e  fotoperíodo natural. Após a aclimatação, os peixes foram aleatoriamente  divididos em   quatro  grupos (n=10): Caraá, Parobé, Novo   Hamburgo,  os quais foram expostos à água   proveniente  do respectivo ponto de amostragem   no rio,  e um grupo controle mantido em   água da  torneira declorificada.      Após 72  horas de exposição, os animais foram   sacrificados  por secção da medula espinhal   e  através de um corte na região do   pedúnculo  caudal foi coletado sangue para   a  realização da técnica do esfregaço em lâmina   citológica.  As lâminas foram fixadas em   etanol  absoluto por 10 minutos e coradas em   Giemsa  5  por 10 minutos, sendo então lavadas   em água  corrente, codificadas e analisadas   em  microscópio óptico em aumento de   1000x.  Foram analisados 2000 eritrócitos por   animal. Partículas  pequenas, arredondadas   ou  ovais, não refrativas e com o mesmo padrão   de  coloração do núcleo principal foram   consideradas  micronúcleos (Çavas e Ergene-   Gözükara  2005). Alterações na morfologia do   núcleo,  tais como brotamentos, invaginações   e  segmentações foram consideradas anormalidades   nucleares  (Carrasco et al. 1990;  Pacheco   e Santos  1997).      As  frequências de micronúcleos e anormalidades   nucleares  foram comparadas entre os   grupos  expostos à água do rio e o grupo controle.   A  análise estatística foi realizada através   do teste  Kruskal-Wallis, considerando um nível   de  significância de 5  (p<0.05). O programa   utilizado  foi o Statistical  Package for the   Social  Sciences (SPSS)  22.0.      Resultados      Os resultados  obtidos na análise de parâmetros   físico-químicos  e microbiológicos das   amostras  de água coletadas são exibidos na   tabela 1. Não  foram detectadas concentrações   de  nitrogênio amoniacal, cobre e cromo   total em  nenhum dos pontos. Todas as   amostras  apresentaram valores de DBO acima   do  limite permitido para águas de classe I   (3 mg O2 L-1)  conforme a resolução CONAMA   357/2005.  Para os demais parâmetros analisados,   Caraá  apresentou todos os resultados   dentro  do limite para a classe I, enquanto Parobé   e Novo  Hamburgo ficaram acima do limite   para  fósforo total, coliformes termotolerantes,   alumínio  e ferro, sendo os maiores valores   registrados  para Novo Hamburgo. O ponto de   Parobé  foi o único em que foi detectado o metal   chumbo e  em concentração acima do limite   para  águas de classe I.     Tabela 1. Discussão      O trecho  superior do rio apresentou, em geral,   parâmetros  físico-químicos e microbiológicos   dentro  dos limites permitidos para águas de   classe I  conforme a resolução brasileira CONAMA   357/2005.  Segundo o Comitesinos   (2000),  essa região apresenta os menores impactos   ambientais  da bacia hidrográfica. Os   trechos  médio e especialmente inferior, por   outro  lado, estão expostos a maiores pressões   antrópicas  (Blume et al. 2010),  de forma   que a  maior quantidade de parâmetros acima   dos  limites de concentração para a classe de   melhor  qualidade de água nessas regiões é   reflexo  dessa situação.     Diversos  estudos já foram realizados na Bacia   Hidrográfica  do Rio dos Sinos visando à avaliação   do  potencial genotóxico de suas águas. Scalon et al. (2013)  revisaram o resultado de alguns  desses estudos, os quais aplicaram diferentes  metodologias, como o teste Salmonella/ Microssoma,  teste de micronúcleos em  linhagem celular, teste Allium cepa, entre outros,  constatando que houve tanto resultados positivos  quanto negativos para efeitos genotóxicos.      Scalon et al. (2010)  propuseram o primeiro experimento   utilizando  biomarcadores de genotoxicidade   em  peixes para avaliar a água do Rio   dos  Sinos, o teste de cometa em eritrócitos de   Hyphessobrycon  luetkenii. Os  autores verificaram   alterações  sazonais na frequência de danos   de DNA  induzida pela água dos trechos   superior e inferior. Scalon et al.  (2013),  também   utilizando  teste de cometa em H. luetkenii, verificaram   efeito  genotóxico na água do trecho médio na coleta de verão e nos três trechos na   coleta  de inverno quando comparados ao grupo   controle.  Bergamaschi et al. (2015) aplicaram o   teste de  micronúcleos e anormalidades nucleares   em  eritrócitos de peixes da espécie Leporinus   obtusidens expostos  à água coletada nos   três  trechos do rio, não encontrando diferenças   significativas  entre esses grupos e o controle.   Bianchi et al. (2015)  aplicaram tanto o teste de   micronúcleos  e anormalidades nucleares quanto   o ensaio  cometa em eritrócitos de Astyanax   jacuhiensis expostos  á água do Rio dos Sinos.   Para a  primeira metodologia, não encontraram   diferenças  entre os trechos analisados, mas para   a  segunda, verificaram aumento na frequência   de danos  ao material genético dos grupos   expostos  à água dos trechos médio e inferior   em  comparação ao trecho superior.      O teste  de micronúcleos em eritrócitos de C.   carpio já foi  utilizado com o objetivo de verificar   o  potencial genotóxico de determinadas   substâncias  (Buschini et al. 2004;  Gustavino   et al. 2005;  Canistro et al. 2012;  García-Medina   et al. 2013)  ou a sensibilidade da espécie   às  mesmas (Al-Sabti 1986; Grisolia e Cordeiro   2000).  São poucos os estudos visando à avaliação   de  corpos de água com a espécie. Grisolia   e  Starling (2001) e Grisolia et al. (2009)   realizaram  o teste em espécimes capturados   no lago  Paranoá, Brasília.      A  ausência de diferença nas frequências de   micronúcleos  e de anormalidades nucleares   entre o  grupo controle e os grupos expostos à   água do  rio indica a ausência de potencial genotóxico   da água  do Rio dos Sinos em C. carpio   no  período amostrado. As baixas frequências   de  micronúcleos nos animais do presente   estudo e  também reportadas na literatura para   a  espécie (Grisolia e Starling 2001; Grisolia   et al. 2009),  podem ser consideradas a taxa   basal  para a espécie e é similar a observada   para a  maioria das espécies de peixes, cujas   médias  variam entre 0 e 1 micronúcleos por   1.000  células (Bolognesi e Hayashi 2011). Este   estudo  foi o primeiro a aplicar o teste de   micronúcleos  em C. carpio para  avaliação da   qualidade  da água do Rio dos Sinos, e, para   que esta  espécie seja utilizada como bioindicadora,   algumas  variações nas condições   experimentais  devem ser testadas, tais como   maiores  períodos de exposição, e também a   análise  de maior número de células, tal como   sugere  Udroiu (2006) para espécies nas quais   as  frequências de micronúcleos são baixas. Address: Highway RS-239, km 2755, Zip Code 93352-000, Novo Hamburgo, RS, Brazil. *mateussouza@feevale.br Received: November 9, 2015 Accepted: September 9, 2016 Abstract. The Rio dos Sinos is located in southern Brazil, is approximately 190 km long, and provides water for agricultural and industrial activities, as well as for the consumption of over one million inhabitants. This river is considered one of the most polluted in Brazil, and therefore studies to evaluate the water quality along its length are necessary. The micronucleus test in fish erythrocytes has been successfully used to detect the presence of mutagenic pollutants in aquatic environments. The aim of this study was to evaluate the water quality of the Sinos River by testing for micronuclei in Cyprinus carpio, as well as by performing physical-chemical and microbiological analyses. Water samples were collected from the upper (Caraá), middle (Parobé) and lower (Novo Hamburgo) stretches of the Sinos River in December 2013. The samples were transported to the laboratory for analysis of 14 water quality parameters, as well as for exposing C. carpio specimens for 72 h in aquariums. No significant differences were observed in the frequency of micronuclei and nuclear abnormalities in the groups exposed to river water compared to the control group. Only one water quality parameter was observed to be in violation of the legislation in the upper stretch of the river, while in the middle and lower stretches there were six and five parameters, respectively. The results demonstrate that the Sinos River presents a reduction in water quality along its length and indicate the absence of genotoxic potential during the sampling period. Keywords: Sinos River; Biomarkers; Water quality; Cyprinus carpio.        Abstract.      The Sinos River is located in South of Brazil, it has about 190 km of extension and provides water for agricultural and industrial activities, and for consumption of more than one million inhabitants. This river is considered one of the most polluted rivers in Brazil;  therefore, studies aiming to evaluate the water quality along its course are necessary. The micronucleus test in fish erythrocytes has been successfully used to detect mutagenic pollutants in the aquatic environment. The objective of this study was to evaluate the water quality of the Sinos River by the micronucleus test in Cyprinus carpio, as well as physicochemical and microbiological analyses. Water samples were collected in the upper (Caraá municipality), middle (Parobé municipality) and lower (Novo Hamburgo municipality) sections of the Sinos River, in December 2013. The samples were transported to the laboratory for analysis of 14 water quality parameters and for exposure of C. carpio for 72 hours in aquaria. Significant differences in micronucleus and nuclear abnormalities frequencies were not found between the control and the exposed groups. Only one parameter of water quality exceeded the limit of the legislation in the upper section of the river, while in the middle and lower sections, six and five parameters, respectively. These results show that the Sinos River presents a reduction in water quality along its extension and indicates the absence of genotoxic potential in the sampled period. Keywords: Sinos river; Biomarkers; Water quality; Cyprinus carpio. Introduction The Sinos River, located in the northeast region of Rio Grande do Sul, is considered one of the main rivers in the state, concentrating a significant percentage of the population in its river basin area, in addition to a large industrial and tourist park (Comitesinos 2000). Along its extension, of approximately 190 km, it provides water for agricultural, industrial and human consumption activities, and is also used as a means of diluting domestic sewage effluents, industrial effluents and waste of rural origin (Bieger et al. 2010). The impacts caused by human activities contribute to the reduction of the water quality of the Sinos River. Monitoring of physical and chemical parameters of the water carried out along the river indicates that this reduction occurs mainly in its lower stretch, close to large urban centers, where there is a higher population and industrial density (Blume et al. 2010). According to the state environmental agency (SEMA 2014), several points along the river were evaluated in classes III and IV of water quality according to the classification established by Brazilian resolution CONAMA 357/2005 (Brazil 2005), in which class I represents the best quality and class IV the worst. In addition to monitoring physical and chemical parameters, several studies have proposed the use of bioindicators as complementary tools in assessing river water quality (Schulz and Martins-Júnior 2001; Rechenmacher et al. 2010; Scalon et al. 2010; Nunes et al. 2011; Scalon et al. 2013; Weber et al. 2013; Bergamaschi et al. 2015; Bianchi et al. 2015). Such studies are important for a broader analysis of the impacts caused by human activities, since they provide the possibility of revealing the toxic potential of water to living organisms. Fish are widely used as bioindicators of aquatic environments, both in situ studies, due to their high availability and important role in the food chain (Oost et al. 2003), and in the laboratory, due to their ease of maintenance and exposure (Al-Sabti and Metcalfe 1995). The test for micronuclei and nuclear abnormalities in fish erythrocytes is a widely used tool for analyzing the genotoxicity of water due to its simplicity and speed of analysis (Bolognesi and Hayashi 2011). Micronuclei are chromosome fragments or entire chromosomes not inserted into the cell nucleus during the division process (Al-Sabti and Metcalfe 1995). Nuclear abnormalities are deformations in the morphology of the nucleus, which are also considered indicators of genotoxic effects (Çavas and Ergene-Gözükara 2005). The species Cyprinus carpio (Linnaeus, 1758) of the Cyprinidae family, popularly known as common carp, is widely used in fish farming in Brazil. It originates from Eastern Europe and Western Asia and was one of the first species to be cultivated in aquaculture. It is currently cultivated on all continents due to its hardiness and ease of breeding (Querol et al. 2005). The species has already been successfully used in genotoxicity assessment studies (Buschini et al. 2004; Gustavino et al. 2005; Canistro et al. 2012; García-Medina et al. 2013). In this context, the objective of the present study was to evaluate the water quality of the Rio dos Sinos by means of the micronucleus test in C. carpio as well as physical-chemical and microbiological analyses. Material and methods Study area The Rio dos Sinos Hydrographic Basin is located northeast of the state of Rio Grande do Sul, between the geographic coordinates of 29° 20' to 30° 10' South latitude and 50° 15' to 51° 20' West longitude. It has an area of ​​approximately 3,800 km², covering, partially or totally, 32 municipalities and an estimated population of 1,249,000 inhabitants (SEMA 2010). The main watercourse of the basin, which gives its name to it, is divided into three sections: upper, 25 km long, characterized by a high bottom slope and rapid water flow; middle, which extends for 125 km and whose altitude varies from 60 m to 5 m in average slope; lower section, approximately 50 km long, where the slope is gentle and the water flow is slow (Comitesinos 2000). The upper section has a low population density and predominantly rural economic activities. In the middle section and especially in the lower section, there are large population and industrial concentrations, with tributaries of the Rio dos Sinos draining large urban centers such as Novo Hamburgo and São Leopoldo. The lower section of the basin is exposed to the greatest anthropogenic pressure and is home to the largest industrial base in the state of Rio Grande do Sul (Figueiredo et al. 2010). Surface water collection In December 2013, surface water samples were collected at three points on the Rio dos Sinos, located in the municipalities of Caraá (29° 45' 44.4" S / 50° 19' 39.8" W), Parobé (29° 41' 10.7" S / 50° 51' 03.4" W) and Novo Hamburgo (29° 44' 12.5" S / 51° 05' 29.1" W), representing the three stretches of the river, upper, middle and lower, respectively (Figure 1). The samples were taken to the laboratory, and the following parameters were analyzed in accordance with the Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater (APHA 1998): biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), chemical oxygen demand (COD), total phosphorus, ammonia nitrogen, suspended solids, total and thermotolerant coliforms, aluminum, lead, copper, total chromium, iron, nickel, and zinc. Figure 1. Location of the study area. Water collection points in the Rio dos Sinos indicated by numbers: 1) Caraá, 2) Parobé, 3) Novo Hamburgo. Experimental procedure The experimental protocol of the present work was approved by the Ethics Committee on the Use of Animals of Feevale University (protocol no. 02.13022). Specimens of C. carpio (n=40) were purchased from a local fish farmer and acclimated for seven days in dechlorinated tap water with constant aeration, in a room with controlled temperature (22±1ºC) and natural photoperiod. After acclimation, the fish were randomly divided into four groups (n=10): Caraá, Parobé, Novo Hamburgo, which were exposed to water from the respective sampling point in the river, and a control group maintained in dechlorinated tap water. After 72 hours of exposure, the animals were sacrificed by sectioning the spinal cord and through a cut in the region of the caudal peduncle, blood was collected for the smear technique on cytological slides. The slides were fixed in absolute ethanol for 10 minutes and stained in Giemsa 5 for 10 minutes, then washed in running water, coded and analyzed under an optical microscope at 1000x magnification. A total of 2000 erythrocytes per animal were analyzed. Small, rounded or oval particles, non-refractive and with the same staining pattern as the main nucleus were considered micronuclei (Çavas and Ergene-Gözükara 2005). Changes in the morphology of the nucleus, such as budding, invaginations and segments were considered nuclear abnormalities (Carrasco et al. 1990; Pacheco and Santos 1997). The frequencies of micronuclei and nuclear abnormalities were compared between the groups exposed to river water and the control group. Statistical analysis was performed using the Kruskal-Wallis test, considering a significance level of 5 (p<0.05). The program used was the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) 22.0. Results The results obtained in the analysis of physical-chemical and microbiological parameters of the collected water samples are shown in Table 1. No concentrations of ammoniacal nitrogen, copper and total chromium were detected at any of the points. All samples presented BOD values ​​above the limit allowed for class I waters (3 mg O2 L-1) according to CONAMA resolution 357/2005. For the other parameters analyzed, Caraá presented all results within the limit for class I, while Parobé and Novo Hamburgo were above the limit for total phosphorus, thermotolerant coliforms, aluminum and iron, with the highest values ​​recorded for Novo Hamburgo. Parobé was the only point where lead was detected and in concentrations above the limit for class I waters. Table 1. Physicochemical and microbiological parameters of water samples from the Rio dos Sinos collected in the cities of Caraá, Parobé and Novo Hamburgo, corresponding to the upper, middle and lower stretches of the river, respectively. For the micronucleus test (Table 2), no significant differences were observed in the comparisons of the frequencies of micronuclei and nuclear abnormalities of the groups exposed to river water in relation to the control group. Table 2. Frequencies of micronuclei (MN) and nuclear abnormalities (AN) in specimens of Cyprinus carpio exposed to water from the Rio dos Sinos. Discussion The upper stretch of the river generally presented physical-chemical and microbiological parameters within the limits permitted for class I waters according to Brazilian resolution CONAMA 357/2005. According to Comitesinos (2000), this region presents the lowest environmental impacts in the river basin. The middle and especially lower stretches, on the other hand, are exposed to greater anthropogenic pressures (Blume et al. 2010), so the greater number of parameters above the concentration limits for the best water quality class in these regions is a reflection of this situation. Several studies have already been carried out in the Rio dos Sinos River Basin aiming to evaluate the genotoxic potential of its waters. Scalon et al. (2013) reviewed the results of some of these studies, which applied different methodologies, such as the Salmonella/Microsome test, micronucleus test in cell lines, Allium cepa test, among others, finding that there were both positive and negative results for genotoxic effects. Scalon et al. (2010) proposed the first experiment using biomarkers of genotoxicity in fish to evaluate the water of the Rio dos Sinos, the comet test in erythrocytes of Hyphessobrycon luetkenii. The authors observed seasonal changes in the frequency of DNA damage induced by water from the upper and lower reaches. Scalon et al. (2013), also using the comet test in H. luetkenii, observed a genotoxic effect in the water from the middle reach in the summer collection and in the three reaches in the winter collection when compared to the control group. Bergamaschi et al. (2015) applied the micronucleus test and nuclear abnormalities in erythrocytes of fish of the species Leporinus obtusidens exposed to water collected in the three reaches of the river, finding no significant differences between these groups and the control. Bianchiet al. (2015) applied both the micronucleus and nuclear abnormalities test and the comet assay to erythrocytes of Astyanax jacuhiensis exposed to water from the Rio dos Sinos. For the first methodology, they found no differences between the analyzed stretches, but for the second, they found an increase in the frequency of damage to the genetic material of the groups exposed to water from the middle and lower stretches compared to the upper stretch. The micronucleus test on erythrocytes of C. carpio has already been used to verify the genotoxic potential of certain substances (Buschini et al. 2004; Gustavino et al. 2005; Canistro et al. 2012; García-Medina et al. 2013) or the sensitivity of the species to them (Al-Sabti 1986; Grisolia and Cordeiro 2000). There are few studies aimed at evaluating water bodies with the species. Grisolia and Starling (2001) and Grisolia et al. (2009) performed the test on specimens captured in Lake Paranoá, Brasília. The absence of difference in the frequencies of micronuclei and nuclear abnormalities between the control group and the groups exposed to river water indicates the absence of genotoxic potential of the water from the Rio dos Sinos in C. carpio during the sampling period. The low frequencies of micronuclei in the animals of the present study and also reported in the literature for the species (Grisolia and Starling 2001; Grisolia et al. 2009) can be considered the basal rate for the species and is similar to that observed for most fish species, whose averages vary between 0 and 1 micronuclei per 1,000 cells (Bolognesi and Hayashi 2011). This study was the first to apply the micronucleus test in C. carpio to evaluate the water quality of the Rio dos Sinos. For this species to be used as a bioindicator, some variations in the experimental conditions should be tested, such as longer exposure periods and the analysis of a larger number of cells, as suggested by Udroiu (2006) for species in which micronucleus frequencies are low. snippet: 27 de abr. de 2015 — ... Porto Alegre, é comum enxergar garrafas, objetos de plástico e até eletrodomésticos. Toda a sujeira vai parar diariamente no Rio Gravataí. É ...
trans_snippet: Apr 27 2015 — ... Porto Alegre, it is common to see bottles, plastic objects and even household appliances. All the dirt ends up daily in the Gravataí River. AND ...
text: Apenas 12  do esgoto é tratado no Rio Grande do Sul. O descontrole já inutilizou metade das águas do Rio Gravataí, na Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre, como mostra a reportagem do RBS Notícias, da RBS TV (veja o vídeo acima). Reveja todas as reportagens da série.   Análises feitas pela Companhia Riograndense de Saneamento (Corsan) mostram que o oxigênio é quase inexistente no rio, com níveis abaixo do recomendado para a vida de peixes e outros seres vivos. Também foi pesquisada a quantidade de coliformes fecais, bactérias que causam doenças. Por lei, o número não deve ultrapassar 1 mil coliformes a cada 100 ml de água. Entretanto, os níveis encontrados foram 142 vezes o volume permitido. Em mais da metade do rio, o recomendado é não entrar em contato com a água.   "A classificação, conforme a legislação federal, são zero, um, dois, três e quatro. A classe zero é a melhor, que se pode usar a água com tratamento primário. A classe um ainda é com tratamento primário. Já a classe dois já requer tratamento secundário com decantação, e a também bastante cuidado. Na classe 4 a legislação diz que não podemos tirar água para consumo humano, apenas como paisagismo e para a função do ecossistema", explica Samuel.   No arroio Passo das Pedras, na Zona Norte de Porto Alegre, é comum enxergar garrafas, objetos de plástico e até eletrodomésticos. Toda a sujeira vai parar diariamente no Rio Gravataí. É a contribuição do esgoto da capital na contaminação do quinto rio mais poluído do Brasil, segundo dados do IBGE.    O que acontece todos os dias no Rio Gravataí é preocupação para a ONG de proteção ambiental Apta há muitos anos. "Pela poluição, exatamente, isso aqui é um esgoto cloacal. O odor daqui é horrível, porque a agua é dejeto puro. Não só cheira como é o próprio esgoto", diz o presidente da ONG, Clóvis Braga.   O que o ambientalista diz foi confirmado pelas análises da Corsan. As coletas foram recomendadas pelo Ministério Público de Gravataí para verificar a qualidade das águas, e os resultados são assustadores. Das classes de um rio, estabelecidas pelo Conselho Nacional do Meio Ambiente, o Gravataí está na pior.   "Ele está classificado em classe 4, onde nós temos reflexo direto da urbanização principalmente pela falta de tratamento de esgotos sanitários", diz o presidente do Comitê de Bacia do Gravataí, engenheiro civil Paulo Robinson da Silva Samuel.   A Bacia do Gravataí é formada pelos municípios de Santo Antônio da Patrulha, Taquara, Glorinha, Gravataí, Cachoeirinha, Alvorada, Viamão, Canoas e Porto Alegre. Entretanto, 90  do esgoto desses nove municípios são jogados brutos no rio, segundo dados do Ministério das Cidades.   A poluição é tanta que a Corsan desativou alguns pontos de captação de água no Gravataí. Para não haver desabastecimento, a alternativa foi retirar a agua do Arroio das Garças, que fica a pouco mais de um quilômetro da foz do Rio Gravataí. Segundo o ambientalista, a situação também pode apresentar risco de contaminação em breve.   "Sendo predominante aqui na região, os vento sul quase que diariamente sopra os dejetos, toda a poluição, os efluentes do Rio Gravataí rumo à Estação de Captação da Corsan. A empresa não capta diretamente, mas está captando a água dessa região, porque indiretamente a água do Gravataí adentra o Arroio das Garças", diz o presidente da ONG Apta.   Entretanto, a direção técnica da Corsan garante a qualidade da água que chega aos consumidores.   "Dos investimentos da Corsan, que chegam a quase R$ 4 bilhões, mais de 80  são relativos a esgotamento sanitário. Portanto, é a preocupação número 1 da empresa fazer com que haja implantação não só de redes de coleta, mas também de tratamentos de esgotos de modo adequado que possam contribuir em preservação e baixo impacto nos nossos corpos receptores", diz o diretor de Operações da companhia, engenheiro químico Eduardo Barbosa de Carvalho.
text_en: Only 12% of the sewage is treated in Rio Grande do Sul. The lack of control has already rendered half of the waters of the Gravataí River, in the Metropolitan Region of Porto Alegre, unusable, as shown in the report by RBS Notícias, from RBS TV (watch the video above). Watch all the reports in the series. Analyses carried out by the Riograndense Sanitation Company (Corsan) show that oxygen is almost non-existent in the river, with levels below those recommended for the life of fish and other living beings. The amount of fecal coliforms, bacteria that cause diseases, was also researched. By law, the number should not exceed 1,000 coliforms per 100 ml of water. However, the levels found were 142 times the permitted volume. In more than half of the river, it is recommended not to come into contact with the water. "The classification, according to federal legislation, is zero, one, two, three and four. Class zero is the best, in which water with primary treatment can be used. Class one is still with primary treatment. Class dThe water already requires secondary treatment with decantation, and also a lot of care. In class 4, the legislation states that we cannot take water for human consumption, only for landscaping and for the ecosystem's function", explains Samuel. In the Passo das Pedras stream, in the North Zone of Porto Alegre, it is common to see bottles, plastic objects and even household appliances. All the dirt ends up in the Gravataí River every day. This is the contribution of the capital's sewage to the contamination of the fifth most polluted river in Brazil, according to data from the IBGE. What happens every day in the Gravataí River has been a concern for the environmental protection NGO Apta for many years. "Because of the pollution, exactly, this here is sewage. The smell here is horrible, because the water is pure waste. It not only smells, it is sewage itself", says the president of the NGO, Clóvis Braga. What the environmentalist says was confirmed by the analyses by Corsan. The collections were recommended by the Public Prosecutor's Office of Gravataí to verify the qualityof the waters, and the results are frightening. Of the river classes established by the National Environmental Council, the Gravataí is in the worst. "It is classified in class 4, where we have a direct impact of urbanization mainly due to the lack of sewage treatment", says the president of the Gravataí Basin Committee, civil engineer Paulo Robinson da Silva Samuel. The Gravataí Basin is formed by the municipalities of Santo Antônio da Patrulha, Taquara, Glorinha, Gravataí, Cachoeirinha, Alvorada, Viamão, Canoas and Porto Alegre. However, 90% of the sewage from these nine municipalities is dumped raw into the river, according to data from the Ministry of Cities. The pollution is so bad that Corsan has deactivated some water collection points in Gravataí. To avoid shortages, the alternative was to take the water from Arroio das Garças, which is just over a kilometer from the mouth of the Gravataí River. According to the environmentalist, the situation may also present a risk of contamination inbrief. "Being predominant here in the region, the south winds almost daily blow the waste, all the pollution, and the effluents from the Gravataí River towards the Corsan Collection Station. The company does not collect water directly, but it is collecting water from this region, because indirectly the water from the Gravataí enters the Arroio das Garças", says the president of the NGO Apta. However, the technical management of Corsan guarantees the quality of the water that reaches consumers. "Of Corsan's investments, which amount to almost R$4 billion, more than 80 are related to sewage. Therefore, the company's number one concern is to ensure that there is implementation not only of collection networks, but also of appropriate sewage treatment that can contribute to preservation and low impact on our receiving bodies", says the company's Operations Director, chemical engineer Eduardo Barbosa de Carvalho.

What happens every day in the Gravataí River has worried the environmental protection NGO APTA for many years. "Because of the pollution, this place is a sewage cesspool. The smell here is horrible, because the water is pure waste. It not only smells, it is sewage itself", says the president of the NGO, Clóvis Braga. What the environmentalist says was confirmed by the analyses by Corsan. The collections were recommended by the Public Prosecutor's Office of Gravataí to verify the quality of the water, and the results are reliablestators. Of the river classes established by the National Environmental Council, the Gravataí is in the worst. "It is classified as class 4, where we have a direct impact of urbanization, mainly due to the lack of sewage treatment," says the executive secretary of the Gravataí Basin Committee, civil engineer Paulo Robinson da Silva Samuel. The Gravataí Basin is made up of the municipalities of Santo Antônio da Patrulha, Taquara, Glorinha, Gravataí, Cachoeirinha, Alvorada, Viamão, Canoas and Porto Alegre. However, 90% of the sewage from these nine municipalities is dumped raw into the river, according to data from the Ministry of Cities. The pollution is so bad that Corsan has deactivated some water collection points in Gravataí. To avoid shortages, the alternative was to take water from Arroio das Garças, which is just over a kilometer from the mouth of the Gravataí River. According to the environmentalist, the situation may also present a risk of contamination soon. "IfThe prevailing wind here in the region blows the waste, all the pollution and effluents from the Gravataí River towards the Corsan Collection Station. The company does not collect water directly, but it is collecting water from this region, because indirectly the water from Gravataí enters the Arroio das Garças", says the president of the NGO Apta. However, the technical management of Corsan guarantees the quality of the water that reaches consumers. "Of Corsan's investments, which amount to almost R$4 billion, more than 80 are related to sewage. Therefore, the company's number 1 concern is to ensure that there is implementation not only of collection networks, but also of adequate sewage treatment that can contribute to preservation and low impact on our receiving bodies", says the company's Operations Director, chemical engineer Eduardo Barbosa de Carvalho. Class identified as polluters of the basin claims to be being used to divert attention from a bigger problem In recentAccording to a survey conducted by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE), Rio Grande do Sul appears three times on the list of the ten most polluted rivers in Brazil. Rio dos Sinos, Gravataí and Rio Caí are in fourth, fifth and eighth place, respectively. The Gravataí basin starts in the marshland, in Santo Antônio da Patrulha, and ends at the Jacuí Delta, between Canoas and Porto Alegre. Running through nine municipalities, the Gravataí Basin is at the center of a controversy involving environmental agencies and rice producers. In a report published by a major media outlet in the state, images taken last January show an agricultural aircraft spraying a rice crop with pesticides and hitting a Permanent Preservation Area, in Banhado Grande, between Glorinha and Viamão. The property had been notified months ago about the damage to the forest and the irregular dumping of pesticides into the water. 2015/2016 Harvest and the Use of the Gravataí Basin As shown in the report, the Gravataí Basin is located in the marshland, in the state of Santo Antônio da Patrulha, in the state of São Paulo.According to IRGA, the metropolitan region is currently made up of 110 rice producers. According to estimates, the 2015/2016 harvest had a planted area in the Gravataí Basin of 11,500 thousand hectares. Of these, 78 are irrigated by dams built on the properties. Only 22 of the crops receive water drawn from the River. In this context, the dams built over the years contribute to the flow of the Gravataí in the summer, the dry season. Tributaries and streams of the Gravataí River The main tributaries of the Gravataí River are the Brigadeiro, Barnabé, Demétrio, Pinto, Passo Grande, Miraguaia, Venturosa, Veadinho, and Chico Lomã streams, all on its right bank; while on its left bank, the Areias, Sarandi, Feijó, Águas Belas, Passo dos Negros, and Alexandrina streams form its tributaries. Studies carried out on land cover, use and occupation indicated that field areas prevail (50.81), followed by crops (19.98), forest (11.12), urban areas (7.65), wetlands (3.96), waterua (2.04 ), wet field (1.06 ), bare soil (2.43 ) and reforestation (0.89 ). In the Gravataí River, which supplies water to 1 million people alone, the stabs arrive through the Águas Belas, Barnabé, Feijó, Areia and Sarandi streams. Instead of life and oxygen, they bring tons of human and animal feces to the riverbed. At the mouth of each of the streams, the water, almost still, reveals itself to be pasty and black. In a stretch estimated at 20 kilometers, between Gravataí and Porto Alegre, one comes across dead dogs and horses. On the banks, sofas, tires, stoves, plastic bottles, garbage bags — hundreds of them — and even refrigerators accumulate.

title: Procesaron a diez funcionarios y empleados públicos ...
snippet: 24 jun 2020 — ... Río Neuquén, entre los años 2016 y 2017. A raíz de publicaciones periodísticas que daban cuenta de la presunta contaminación de los ríos ...
trans_snippet: Jun 24, 2020 — ... Neuquén River, between 2016 and 2017. Following journalistic publications that reported on the alleged contamination of the rivers ...
text: En línea con el requerimiento de la titular de la Fiscalía Federal N°2 de Neuquén, María Cristina Beute, el juez federal Gustavo Villanueva procesó sin prisión preventiva a diez funcionarios y empleados de la Provincia de Neuquén, investigados en sendas causas por verter residuos peligrosos desde las Plantas de Tratamiento de Efluentes Cloacales (PTEC) Parque Industrial Norte (PIN) y Bardas Norte y contaminar el Río Neuquén, entre los años 2016 y 2017. A raíz de publicaciones periodísticas que daban cuenta de la presunta contaminación de los ríos Limay y Neuquén, la Fiscalía inició una investigación preliminar el 22 de diciembre de 2016, a fin de determinar si funcionarios y/o empleados del Ente Provincial de Agua y Saneamiento (EPAS) de la Provincia de Neuquén habrían contaminado de un modo peligroso para la salud parte de un tramo del cauce del río Neuquén -que baña un lateral de la capital provincial y opera como límite con la Provincia de Río Negro- mediante el vertido de efluentes cloacales desde la Planta de Tratamiento de Efluentes Cloacales Parque Industrial Norte (PIN), y desde la Planta de Tratamiento de Efluentes Cloacales Bardas Norte. Así, el 22 de mayo de 2017, en el marco de las respectivas investigaciones, se tomaron muestras de agua del curso del río en los puntos de vertido y se constató contaminación por presencia de coliformes totales y fecales, escherichia coli, plomo, nitrógeno amoniacal, fósforo y nitrógeno, sustancias peligrosas en los términos de la Ley 24.051.  Asimismo, se consideró que la conducta imputada también vulneró el artículo 5° de la Ley provincial N°1.875, al haber volcado efluentes en el Río Neuquén que contenían agentes químicos y biológicos en cantidades tales que afectarían a la flora, la fauna y la salud humana. Procesamientos En virtud de las pruebas recolectadas, se imputó e indagó a diez funcionarios y empleados del EPAS, responsables de ambas plantas de tratamiento, por haber contaminado el Río Neuquén por el vertido de las plantas de tratamiento Bardas Norte y Parque Industrial Norte. Así, en línea con el requerimiento de la representante del Ministerio Público Fiscal, el juez Villanueva dispuso el procesamiento de los diez involucrados, en orden al artículo 56° de la Ley 24.051 que sanciona a quien, por inobservancia de los reglamentos a su cargo, “utilizando los residuos a que se refiere la presente ley, envenenare, adulterare o contaminare de un modo peligroso para la salud, el suelo, el agua, la atmosfera o el ambiente en general”. Para el juez, las falencias son "el resultado de un accionar desaprensivo para con sus deberes de funcionarios públicos especialmente designados para la protección del medio ambiente en general” En tal sentido, el magistrado señaló que “En efecto, las falencias que se observaron en la planta de tratamiento y aquellas que, si bien no se observaron empíricamente, surgieron del resultado de los análisis elaborados, no son más que el resultado de un accionar desaprensivo para con sus deberes de funcionarios públicos especialmente designados para la protección del medio ambiente en general”. Y agregó que el resultado de las muestras obtenidas y la inspección ocular también “son reveladores de que no ejercieron adecuadamente el poder de policía y de seguridad técnica sobre los sistemas de tratamiento de los líquidos cloacales”, ni tampoco aseguraron el funcionamiento adecuado de ambas plantas de tratamiento. Asimismo, se les trabó embargos sobre sus bienes hasta cubrir la suma de $50.000, cada uno, en las dos investigaciones en las que fueron procesados.
text_en: In line with the request of the head of the Federal Prosecutor's Office No. 2 of Neuquén, María Cristina Beute, federal judge Gustavo Villanueva prosecuted without preventive detention ten officials and employees of the Province of Neuquén, investigated in separate cases for dumping hazardous waste from the Sewage Effluent Treatment Plants (PTEC) Parque Industrial Norte (PIN) and Bardas Norte and contaminating the Neuquén River, between 2016 and 2017. Following newspaper publications that reported the alleged contamination of the Limay and Neuquén rivers, the Prosecutor's Office began a preliminary investigation on December 22, 2016, in order to determine whether officials and/or employees of the Provincial Water and Sanitation Agency (EPAS) of the Province of Neuquén had contaminated in a manner dangerous to health part of a section of the Neuquén River - which flows along one side of the provincial capital and operates as a border with the Province of Río Negro - by means of the Discharge of sewage effluent from the Parque Industrial Norte (PIN) Sewage Effluent Treatment Plant and from the Bardas Norte Sewage Effluent Treatment Plant. Thus, on May 22, 2017, as part of the respective investigations, water samples were taken from the riverbed at the discharge points and contamination was confirmed due to the presence of total and fecal coliforms, Escherichia coli, lead, ammoniacal nitrogen, phosphorus and nitrogen, hazardous substances under the terms of Law 24,051. Likewise, it was considered that the imputed conduct also violated Article 5 of Provincial Law No. 1,875, by having dumped effluent into the Neuquén River that contained chemical and biological agents in quantities such that they would affect flora, fauna and human health. Prosecutions Based on the evidence collected, ten EPAS officials and employees responsible for both treatment plants were charged and investigated for having contaminated the Neuquén River by the discharge of the Bardas Norte and Parque Industrial Norte treatment plants. Thus, in line with the request of the representative of the Public Prosecutor's Office, Judge Villanueva ordered the prosecution of the ten involved, in accordance with article 56 of Law 24,051, which penalizes anyone who, by failing to comply with the regulations in charge, "using the waste referred to in this law, poisons, adulterates or contaminates in a manner dangerous to health, soil, water, the atmosphere or the environment in general." For the judge, the deficiencies are "the result of reckless behavior towards their duties as public officials specially designated for the protection of the environment in general." In this regard, the magistrate pointed out that "Indeed, the deficiencies observed in the treatment plant and those that, although not observed empirically, arose from the results of the analyses carried out, are nothing more than the result of reckless behavior towards their duties as public officials specially designated for the protection of the environment in general." He added that the results of the samples obtained and the visual inspection also "reveal that they did not adequately exercise the power of police and technical security over the sewage treatment systems," nor did they ensure the proper functioning of both treatment plants. Likewise, seizures were placed on their assets up to the sum of $50,000 each, in the two investigations in which they were prosecuted.

text: La Autoridad Interjurisdiccional de las Cuencas de los ríos Limay, Neuquén y Negro (AIC) realizó controles de aptitud de las aguas del Río Limay en Plottier y aseguró que están aptas para su uso recreativo.Los análisis los realizó en el balneario camping Nepen-Hué y en La Herradura, y según informó la Municipalidad en ambos sectores los niveles dieron aptos.Para este control se determinó en muestras de agua la densidad de la bacteria Escherichia coli. text_en: The Interjurisdictional Authority of the Limay, Neuquén and Negro River Basins (AIC) carried out suitability checks on the waters of the Limay River in Plottier and confirmed that they are suitable for recreational use. The analyses were carried out at the Nepen-Hué camping resort and in La Herradura, and according to the Municipality, the levels in both sectors were suitable. For this control, the density of the Escherichia coli bacteria was determined in water samples. The international indicator taken as a reference considers suitable for recreational use, the waters in which the geometric mean calculated from 5 analyses carried out in a period of no more than 30 days and that does not exceed 200 Escherichia Coli per 100ml. The results both in the Camping, as in La Herradura were the following: For the camping: Geometric mean (G) NMP/100ml (27) - Qualification: PASS and for La Herradura: Geometric mean (G) NMP/100ml (25) - Qualification: PASS.
